accepted_regressions: Validation's case-averaged fraction exceeding 5L rises from 0.06399% to 0.08738%, an increase of 0.02338 percentage points or 36.5%, despite the slightly better average P99.9. This is a real aggregate tail-frequency regression.

Val2 P99.9/L rises from 2.482 to 6.539, or 163.5%. Errors exceeding 5L increase from 48/275647 paired reads (0.01741%) to 554/285340 (0.19415%), an 11.15-fold frequency increase. This recurring regression is accepted against a 26.501-point core-error improvement and 51.9% lower MAE/L.

Val11 P99/L rises from 1.925 to 2.718 and P99.9/L from 6.456 to 7.318. Errors exceeding 5L increase from 185/155969 (0.11861%) to 644/156657 (0.41109%); they now contribute 11.3% of paired absolute error. These substantial tail costs are outweighed by a 23.401-point core-error improvement and 62.3% lower MAE/L.

Training gap_sssp P99/L rises from 1.861 to 4.336, with errors exceeding 5L increasing from 2729/373240 (0.7312%) to 2895/375577 (0.7708%). Whiskey P99/L rises from 2.134 to 2.871, with the corresponding frequency rising from 305/158540 (0.1924%) to 423/159317 (0.2655%). Their MAE/L improves by 46.0% and 64.4%, respectively. Whisper P99.9/L also rises from 2.146 to 2.662, despite better core error, MAE/L, P99 and 1L exceedance frequency.

Other validation regressions include val14 P99/L increasing from 2.169 to 3.128; val8 P99.9/L from 4.396 to 4.693; and val13 P99.9/L from 2.284 to 2.623. Val13 has three errors exceeding 5L among 22475 pairs, versus zero among 22464 previously, limiting conclusions about recurrence. Val9's 5L frequency rises slightly from 0.02656% to 0.02800%; its count increase from 475 to 562 accompanies a substantially larger paired population.
contract_findings: Source inspection found no demonstrated contract violation. The candidate computes one completion cycle from the current admission, hardware configuration and retained historical state. It exposes no path to revise issued predictions, inspect future requests or oracle internals, or branch on workload or evaluation identity.

The implementation maintains aggregate bank, bank-group and channel work estimates plus bounded row-history summaries. It does not retain pending transactions, select commands or execute a command-event schedule. Hardware-derived activation/precharge costs, row-cycle service, column spacing and transfer work provide physical interpretations for these approximations.

Parameters control bank and bus service scaling, admission overhead and amortized write-turnaround cost. Both supplied parameter files are empty, so declared defaults apply. Hardware topology indexing and historical row comparisons do not demonstrate specialization to particular addresses.
improvements: Training case-averaged absolute core error falls from 23.669% to 4.266%, improving 19.403 percentage points or 82.0%. Request MAE/L falls from 54.250% to 22.525% of L, improving 31.726 points or 58.5%.

Validation case-averaged absolute core error falls from 24.903% to 7.681%, improving 17.222 percentage points or 69.2%. Request MAE/L falls from 53.086% to 25.981% of L, improving 27.106 points or 51.1%. These gains occur in every case, rather than depending on pooled request counts.

Mean absolute per-case signed drift/L falls from 54.250% to 6.650% in training and from 53.086% to 13.273% in validation. Signed means improve from -54.250% to -6.266% and from -53.086% to -12.181%, respectively. Absolute-error improvements independently support the bias gains.

Case-averaged P99 absolute error/L improves from 2.407 to 1.725 in training and 2.016 to 1.563 in validation. P99.9 improves from 4.377 to 3.379 and 3.493 to 3.394. Mean fractions exceeding 1L fall from 16.822% to 5.964% and from 12.290% to 6.098%.

Mean oracle matching coverage increases from 95.583% to 96.313% in training and 94.246% to 96.135% in validation. For example, val9 coverage rises from 86.286% to 96.827% while MAE/L decreases. The broad gains therefore do not coincide with broadly reduced measurement coverage.
decision.rationale: No demonstrated contract violation was found. Across all 14 training and all 14 anonymized validation cases in the required single-core group, both core error and request MAE/L improve. The incumbent and stage-entry reference are identical, so both comparisons support promotion. Large, consistent primary-objective gains outweigh the documented tail regressions, although serious individual-case failures remain.

uncertainty: No separate mechanical integrity verdict was supplied. Source inspection cannot establish that those authoritative checks passed. No conflicting mechanical result was present.

Persistent individual-core failures remain: val3 is still 44.380% too fast, with MAE/L 0.5382 and signed drift/L -0.5367 across 177720 pairs at 99.660% coverage. Training lbm remains 18.388% too fast, with MAE/L 0.5629. Val9 and val10 retain substantial negative drift as well.

Small signed bias or core error does not imply accurate individual requests. Arizona has signed drift/L approximately -0.0002 but MAE/L 0.3784; val2 has only 0.234% core error but MAE/L 0.2718 and the documented recurring tail regression.

Candidate oracle matching coverage ranges from 90.297% to 99.803% in training and 87.576% to 99.768% in validation. Coverage declines slightly for gap_bfs, val4 and val5; unmatched errors remain unknown. All candidate model admissions have recorded latency, but three training and six validation oracle admissions lack recorded latency. Improved coverage does not establish identical paired populations or complete-admission accuracy.

No synthetic or replay diagnostic results were supplied. From the equations, streaming behavior depends on row reuse and accumulated transfer work, while dependent-random behavior with little overlap relies primarily on base latency and activation/precharge estimates. These are mechanistic expectations, not verified explanations of measured failures. The model omits explicit refresh and approximates write batching and row residency. No complete-admission causal replay claim is supported.

Only the single-core group is required and supplied for this stage. Four- and eight-core accuracy, repeat-run variability, and comparative performance against the other named baselines are not established by this evidence.

accepted_regressions: Case-averaged P99 absolute error/L rises from 1.725 to 1.793 in training, or 3.9%, and from 1.563 to 1.601 in validation, or 2.4%. P99.9/L rises from 3.379 to 3.463 and from 3.394 to 3.717, respectively. Mean fractions exceeding 5L increase from 0.11086% to 0.12943% in training (+0.01857 percentage points; 16.7%) and from 0.08738% to 0.10311% in validation (+0.01573 points; 18.0%). Mean 1L exceedance fractions also rise, from 5.964% to 6.123% and from 6.098% to 6.106%.

Training MAE/L increases by 1.258 percentage points in arizona, 1.587 in charlie, 0.432 in gap_sssp and 0.430 in whiskey, corresponding to relative increases of 3.3%, 3.1%, 1.2% and 2.0%. Arizona signed drift/L worsens from -0.020% to +10.626%; its improved core error does not establish improved request accuracy.

Recurring training tails worsen. Whiskey errors exceeding 5L rise from 423/159317 pairs (0.2655%) to 669/159395 (0.4197%), a 58.1% frequency increase; P99/L rises from 2.871 to 3.388. Gap_sssp exceeds 5L on 2957/375678 pairs (0.7871%), versus 2895/375577 (0.7708%); these errors contribute 14.4% of its paired absolute error. Bravo's corresponding count rises from 128 to 202 among approximately 1.032 million pairs. These are recurring costs, rather than isolated maxima.

The largest primary gains also carry tail costs. Whisper P99.9/L rises from 2.662 to 3.386, and its 1L exceedance frequency rises from 1.170% to 1.920%. Val10 P99.9/L rises from 0.696 to 1.088, with 1L exceedances increasing from 66/248036 to 433/249258. Val9 P99.9/L rises from 1.638 to 2.637, although its 5L frequency improves from 0.02800% to 0.02640% and its count falls from 562 to 546 despite more pairs.

Val2 core error rises from 0.234% to 0.959% (+0.725 percentage points), MAE/L rises from 27.185% to 27.306%, and signed drift/L rises from +5.466% to +9.866%. P99.9/L increases from 6.539 to 7.165; errors exceeding 5L rise from 554/285340 pairs (0.1942%) to 690/290983 (0.2371%). The frequency increase persists after accounting for the larger population.

Validation tails worsen further in val11, val14 and val8. Their 5L frequencies increase from 0.4111% to 0.4771% (644/156657 to 748/156768 pairs), from 0.2962% to 0.3467% (837/282568 to 981/282991), and from 0.0693% to 0.0960% (158/227909 to 219/228190). Their P99/L values increase from 2.718 to 3.154, 3.128 to 3.486, and 2.040 to 2.222. These regressions are accepted against the overall primary-objective benefit, not because local mean gains eliminate the tail costs.

Other primary regressions are small in absolute terms: val4, val5, val7 and val13 MAE/L increase by 0.189, 0.515, 0.087 and 0.104 percentage points. Core error increases by 0.109 points in val6, 0.203 in val12, 0.065 in gms_maxclique and 0.0024 in gms_kstar. Val13 P99.9/L rises from 2.623 to 3.495, with 5L exceedances increasing from 3/22475 to 11/22476; the small count limits recurrence estimates.

Cumulative validation tail deterioration remains material relative to stage entry: mean 5L frequency rises from 0.06399% to 0.10311%, or 61.1%, and mean P99.9/L rises from 3.493 to 3.717. Val2's 5L frequency is now 13.6 times its stage-entry value. Training mean 5L frequency remains 48.5% below stage entry.
contract_findings: Inspection of the supplied candidate source and API found no demonstrated violation. Prediction uses the current admission, hardware configuration and historical state, returning one absolute future cycle. The implementation contains no mechanism to revise issued predictions, inspect future requests or oracle internals, or branch on workload or evaluation identity. Topology indexing and historical row comparisons do not demonstrate address specialization.

Bank, bank-group and channel timestamps represent accumulated service estimates; taking their maximum approximates overlapping resource delays. Last-row, access-class and eight-entry row histories approximate locality and batching. There are no pending transaction objects, command selection or command-event execution. The added read-run counter estimates active-row time consumed by read columns and reduces subsequent row-cycle demand subject to a read-recovery, precharge and activation floor. This remains an admission-based approximation.

The candidate additionally recognizes nCCDL and nWTRL timing keys before their alternate spellings. Bank and bus scales control estimated service demand, admission_overhead adds fixed cycles, and write_batch amortizes turnaround work. Both parameter files are empty, so defaults apply. The implementation itself supports these interpretations; source comments were not treated as authoritative evidence.
improvements: Training mean absolute core error falls from 4.266% to 3.466%, improving 0.799 percentage points or 18.7%. Request MAE/L falls from 22.525% to 20.609% of L, improving 1.915 points or 8.5%. These headlines weight cases equally.
Validation mean absolute core error falls from 7.681% to 6.053%, improving 1.629 percentage points or 21.2%. Request MAE/L falls from 25.981% to 21.485% of L, improving 4.496 points or 17.3%.

Training whisper core error improves from 5.057% to 0.426%, and MAE/L from 33.623% to 8.140%, a 75.8% relative reduction. Lbm core error improves by 3.408 points, from 18.388% to 14.980%, although its MAE/L improves only 0.3% relatively. Llama7b MAE/L falls 66.5%, with an identical paired population.

Validation val9 core error improves from 12.728% to 0.111%, and MAE/L falls 92.4%, from 25.860% to 1.964%. Val10 core error improves from 9.329% to 0.059%, and MAE/L falls 96.0%, from 34.958% to 1.402%. Their oracle matching coverage increases from 96.827% to 99.767% and from 99.094% to 99.582%, respectively.

Mean absolute per-case signed drift/L improves from 6.650% to 4.769% in training and from 13.273% to 8.710% in validation. Signed averages move from -6.266% to -1.905% and from -12.181% to -6.188%. The independent MAE reductions support these bias gains, although individual cases still exhibit cancellation.

Against stage entry, training core error improves from 23.669% to 3.466%, a 20.203-point or 85.4% reduction; MAE/L improves from 54.250% to 20.609%, a 62.0% reduction. Validation core error improves from 24.903% to 6.053%, an 18.850-point or 75.7% reduction; MAE/L improves from 53.086% to 21.485%, a 59.5% reduction.
decision.rationale: No demonstrated contract violation was found. Across the required single-core group, the candidate improves case-averaged core error and request MAE/L in both training and anonymized validation. Core error improves in 12/14 training and 11/14 validation cases; MAE/L improves in 10/14 and 9/14. Large gains in training whisper and validation val9/val10, supported by increased matching coverage, outweigh the documented recurring tail regressions and smaller primary-objective regressions. Every case remains better than stage entry on both primary objectives. Serious individual-case failures remain.

Excluding val9/val10, validation core error improves from 7.123% to 7.047% and MAE/L from 25.243% to 24.786%. These descriptive exclusions show that the headline improvements are not uniform.

Val3 remains essentially unchanged at -44.380% core error, MAE/L 0.5377 and signed drift/L -0.5361 across 177897 pairs at 99.759% coverage. Only six errors exceed 1L, illustrating that a severe widespread bias can evade that threshold. Val7 remains 19.850% too fast, with 76836/433023 errors exceeding 1L. Training lbm remains 14.980% too fast, with MAE/L 0.5612 and 138160/920669 errors exceeding 1L. Charlie's small signed drift/L of -0.0172 coexists with MAE/L 0.5299.

Mean oracle matching coverage increases from 96.313% to 96.391% in training and from 96.135% to 96.552% in validation. Training coverage declines slightly in arizona, cactu and gms_kstar; every validation case gains coverage. Candidate coverage ranges from 90.341% to 99.803% in training and 87.638% to 99.801% in validation. Unmatched errors remain unknown, and improved coverage does not establish identical paired populations. All model admissions have recorded latency; three training and six validation oracle admissions lack it.

No synthetic or replay diagnostic results were supplied. Mechanistically, streaming traffic can exercise column spacing, transfer backlog and the new read-run credit. Dependent-random traffic with little overlap relies primarily on base latency and row activation/precharge once backlog drains. These expectations do not identify validation inputs or establish the causes of measured failures. Refresh is not explicitly modeled, and row residency and write batching remain approximate. Complete-admission causal replay accuracy is not established.

Only the single-core group is required and supplied for this round. Four- and eight-core behavior, repeat-run variability, and comparisons with the other named baselines are not established by this evidence.

accepted_regressions: Training mean P99/L increases from 1.793 to 1.812, or 1.1%; validation mean P99.9/L increases from 3.717 to 3.827, or 3.0%. Mean 5L exceedance frequencies improve only slightly: 0.12943% to 0.12771% in training and 0.10311% to 0.10282% in validation. Relative to stage entry, validation's 5L frequency remains 60.7% higher and P99.9/L 9.6% higher. Those cumulative tail costs remain material.

Val7 MAE/L rises from 51.025% to 53.008%, increasing 1.983 percentage points or 3.9%. Errors exceeding 1L increase from 76836/433023 pairs (17.744%) to 84180/433724 (19.409%), a 9.4% frequency increase that cannot be explained by population growth. This is accepted alongside a 6.743-point core-error improvement, lower P99 and P99.9, and fewer 5L exceedances: 712 to 636.

Val2 core error rises from 0.959% to 1.971%, increasing 1.011 percentage points or 105.4%. Signed drift/L worsens from +9.866% to +11.871%, while MAE/L improves only 0.062 points. Its 5L frequency is essentially unchanged at 0.2374%, but remains about 13.6 times its stage-entry value.

Val9 has a recurring extreme-error regression: 5L exceedances rise from 546/2068182 pairs (0.02640%) to 802/2068180 (0.03878%), increasing 46.9% with virtually identical populations. These errors contribute 16.3% of candidate paired absolute error. P99.9/L rises from 2.637 to 3.012, or 14.2%; MAE/L rises from 1.964% to 2.096%, and core error from 0.111% to 0.188%.

Val12 P99.9/L increases from 2.528 to 4.000, or 58.2%, across the same 80885 pairs. MAE/L increases by 0.188 percentage points, or 4.5%, and core error by 0.021 points. Its 1L exceedance count rises from 1566 to 1574, with no 5L exceedances. The percentile regression concerns the upper distribution, not merely its maximum.

Training whisper worsens on both primary objectives: core error rises from 0.426% to 0.569%, and MAE/L from 8.140% to 9.045%, increasing 0.905 points or 11.1%. P99/L rises 25%, from 1.468 to 1.836. Errors exceeding 1L increase from 2582/134470 pairs (1.920%) to 3422/134460 (2.545%), a 32.5% frequency increase.

Bias and local tails do not improve uniformly. Training's signed mean drift/L moves from -1.905% to +2.508%, increasing its magnitude despite improved mean absolute per-case drift. Arizona drift rises from +10.626% to +14.248%; charlie moves from -1.723% to +9.597%, with 1L exceedances increasing from 14.455% to 15.212%. Val11 drift rises from +0.817% to +6.157%, and val4 from -2.060% to +4.529%. Their improved primary metrics do not erase these costs.

Other primary regressions are small in absolute terms: training mcf core error increases by 0.181 points, gms_maxclique by 0.0066 points, and llama7b MAE/L by 0.0129 points. Validation core error increases by 0.089 points in val1, 0.027 in val13, and less than 0.001 each in val6 and val10. Val13's 5L count rises from 11 to 13 among 22476 pairs, despite improved MAE and percentiles; this small count limits conclusions about recurrence.
contract_findings: Inspection of the supplied candidate source and API found no demonstrated violation. Prediction uses the current admission, hardware configuration and retained historical state, returning one absolute future cycle. There is no mechanism to revise issued predictions, access future traffic or oracle internals, or branch on workload or evaluation identity. Decoded topology indexing and historical row comparisons do not demonstrate address specialization.

Bank, bank-group and channel accumulators estimate outstanding resource work; their maximum approximates overlapping delays. Last-row, access-class and bounded row histories estimate locality and batching. The implementation contains no pending transaction queue, command selection or command-event execution.

The added correction derives write-recovery demand from write latency, burst length, write recovery, precharge and activation timings. Previous admission age and estimated backlog taper that demand. This is a historical admission-based approximation; its equations do not establish that a physical write actually began at the inferred time.

Both parameter files are empty. Defaults therefore apply: bank and bus service scales of 1, one cycle of admission overhead, and turnaround work amortized over 12 writes. These physical interpretations follow from the executable expressions, rather than treating source comments as verified evidence.

No separate mechanical integrity verdict or current frozen-source identity receipt is supplied. Source inspection cannot certify those authoritative checks, and no conflicting mechanical finding is present.
improvements: Training mean absolute core error falls from 3.466% to 0.737%, improving 2.730 percentage points or 78.7%. Request MAE/L falls from 20.609% to 18.115% of L, improving 2.494 points or 12.1%. These are equally weighted case averages.

Validation mean absolute core error falls from 6.053% to 2.649%, improving 3.403 percentage points or 56.2%. MAE/L falls from 21.485% to 17.393%, improving 4.092 points or 19.0%. Excluding val3, core error still improves from 3.104% to 1.925%, and MAE/L from 19.002% to 17.600%.

Major training improvements include gap_bfs core error falling from 11.327% to 0.347% and MAE/L from 29.806% to 14.497%; gap_sssp core error falling from 8.434% to 1.689%; charlie from 7.495% to 1.066%; and lbm from 14.980% to 4.315%. Their respective MAE/L reductions are 51.4%, 17.5%, 10.3% and 3.6%.

Val3 core error improves from 44.380% to 12.066%, a 32.314-point or 72.8% reduction. MAE/L falls from 53.769% to 14.706%, and signed drift/L from -53.613% to -14.348%. Matching coverage increases slightly, from 99.759% to 99.778%. Val4, val8, val11 and val14 also improve both primary objectives; val5 MAE/L improves by 7.506 points.

Mean absolute per-case signed drift/L improves from 4.769% to 4.214% in training and from 8.710% to 4.736% in validation. Mean fractions exceeding 1L fall from 6.123% to 4.797% and from 6.106% to 5.231%, respectively. Training mean P99.9/L improves from 3.463 to 3.387; validation mean P99/L improves from 1.601 to 1.577.

Against stage entry, training core error improves from 23.669% to 0.737%, a 22.932-point or 96.9% reduction, and MAE/L improves from 54.250% to 18.115%, or 66.6%. Validation core error improves from 24.903% to 2.649%, a 22.254-point or 89.4% reduction, and MAE/L improves from 53.086% to 17.393%, or 67.2%.

Mean oracle matching coverage increases from 96.391% to 96.403% in training and from 96.552% to 96.577% in validation. Total paired populations increase by 317 and 2184 reads, respectively. These counts support the coverage assessment; they are not used to pool or reweight accuracy headlines.
decision.rationale: No demonstrated contract violation was found. Across the required single-core group, substantial improvements in case-averaged core error and request MAE/L outweigh the documented regressions. Core error improves in 10/14 training and 7/14 validation cases; MAE/L improves in 11/14 cases in each cohort. Validation gains remain meaningful when the largest improvement, val3, is excluded. Every case improves on both primary objectives relative to stage entry. Coverage does not broadly decline, although serious individual-case failures and recurring tails remain.

contract_findings: Source and API inspection found no demonstrated violation. Prediction uses the current admission, hardware configuration and historical state, returning one absolute future cycle. There is no path to revise issued predictions, inspect future requests or oracle internals, or branch on workload or evaluation identity. Historical row comparisons and decoded topology indexing do not demonstrate address specialization.

The addition maintains one activation-work accumulator per rank and channel. Each estimated new-row access charges max(nRRDS, nFAW/4), with alternate-key fallbacks, and residual work can delay the request's row-access estimate. This approximates activation throughput and the average four-activation power limit. It contains no ACT objects, pending transaction queue, command selection or command-event execution.

Existing bank, bank-group and channel accumulators estimate resource work; their maximum approximates overlapping delays. Row histories approximate locality, while read-run and write-recovery expressions approximate residual bank occupancy. Both parameter files are empty: bank and bus scales default to 1, admission overhead to one cycle, and turnaround work is amortized over 12 writes. These interpretations follow from executable expressions, not source comments.

No separate authoritative mechanical-integrity verdict or current frozen-source identity receipt is supplied. No mechanical failure is reported, but source inspection cannot certify that those checks passed.

Validation mean core error changes from 2.649315% to 2.648619%, improving only 0.000696 points or 0.0263%. Mean P99/L improves slightly from 1.577221 to 1.576599. These are negligible changes, not evidence of substantial validation benefit.

decision.rationale: No demonstrated contract violation was found. This is a modest, concentrated improvement: training bravo improves materially on both primary objectives, and cactu improves request MAE/L despite worse core error and bias. Across all 14 training cases, both primary averages improve; across all 14 anonymized validation cases, performance is effectively unchanged. The localized gains outweigh the documented small regressions. Large improvements over stage entry remain, but those mostly inherited gains are not the justification for this promotion.

decision.rationale: No demonstrated contract violation was found. Across all 14 training and 14 anonymized validation cases in the required single-core group, the candidate provides modest but convincing improvements in request MAE/L, absolute per-case bias and recurring tails. These gains outweigh the small aggregate core-error regressions, although several individual cases worsen. Matching coverage remains essentially stable. uncertainty: Bias provides no independent support for promotion. Mean absolute per-case drift/L rises from 3.97729% to 4.06903% in training (+0.09173 points; 2.31%) and from 4.50091% to 4.50849% in validation. Signed averages rise from +2.24467% to +2.33787% and from +2.16739% to +2.21057%. Gap_bfs drift increases from +2.33067% to +3.09209%. Small core errors elsewhere do not establish unbiased request predictions.

Tail changes are mixed and small. Mean P99/L worsens from 1.75522 to 1.75660 in training and from 1.51606 to 1.51727 in validation. Training mean P99.9/L also worsens slightly. Case-averaged 5L frequency rises from 0.10755% to 0.10800% in training and falls from 0.09122% to 0.09105% in validation; corresponding 1L frequencies change from 4.68143% to 4.67586% and from 5.12015% to 5.12381%.

Val7 remains a serious failure despite its 0.02410-point core improvement: it is still 13.14512% too fast. MAE/L worsens from 53.38443% to 53.44092%, and 1L exceedances rise from 86079/433740 pairs (19.84576%) to 86242/433738 (19.88343%). The frequency increase accompanies a slightly smaller population. Val8's 1L exceedances also increase from 15542 to 15596 despite better MAE and P99.9.

Val3 is unchanged at -12.06557% core error, MAE/L 14.70644% and drift/L -14.34784% across 177930 pairs. Only six errors exceed 1L, illustrating how threshold counts can miss widespread underprediction. Training lbm remains 4.64727% too fast, with MAE/L 54.04193% and 132439/920704 errors exceeding 1L.

Recurring extremes remain substantial: gap_sssp has 2758/375651 errors exceeding 5L, contributing 16.74% of paired absolute error; val11 has 688/156785, contributing 14.38%; val9 has an unchanged count of 837 among 2068181 pairs, contributing 16.74%. Val9's -21.86L extreme is not treated as sufficient evidence by itself. Relative to stage entry, validation mean 5L frequency remains 42.28% higher and mean P99.9/L 6.39% higher.

Coverage is essentially stable, but paired populations are not proven identical. Mean oracle coverage changes from 96.41163% to 96.41082% in training and from 96.57921% to 96.57891% in validation; total pairs change by +6 and -19. Candidate coverage ranges from 90.358% to 99.803% in training and 87.648% to 99.801% in validation. Admission counts and oracle normalization L are unchanged versus the incumbent. Unmatched errors remain unknown. All model admissions have recorded latency; three training and six validation oracle admissions lack it, with no final drain.

No synthetic or replay diagnostic results are supplied, and diagnostic status reports no running job. Mechanistically, streaming traffic exercises transfer backlog, row reuse and direction changes; the new confidence factor attenuates recovery under deep backlog. Sparse dependent-random reads allow accumulated work to drain, leaving intrinsic row-access latency dominant unless a preceding write leaves residual recovery. These expectations do not verify the causes of measured changes. Complete-admission causal replay accuracy is unestablished.

Only the required single-core group is supplied for this round. Four- and eight-core accuracy, repeat-run variability and separate comparisons against all named baselines are unestablished. Actual row residency, write-drain order and activation timing remain approximate; refresh is not explicitly modeled.

contract_findings: No authoritative mechanical-integrity verdict or current frozen-source identity receipt is supplied. No mechanical failure is reported, but source inspection cannot certify that those checks passed.

Inspection of the supplied API and both implementations found no demonstrated violation. The candidate computes one future completion cycle from the current admission, hardware configuration and historical state. There is no mechanism to revise issued predictions, access future traffic or oracle internals, or branch on workload or evaluation identity. Topology indexing and historical row comparisons do not demonstrate address specialization.

Bank, bank-group, rank and channel accumulators estimate residual resource work; their maximum approximates overlapping delays. Bounded row histories approximate locality and batching. The candidate feeds shared-resource delay into the bank accumulator and credits that delay toward elapsed read-row active time. It retains no pending transaction queue and performs no command selection or command-event execution.

Both parameter files are empty. Defaults apply: bank and bus service scales of 1, one cycle of admission overhead, and turnaround work amortized over 12 writes. Hardware timings determine activation, precharge, recovery, column and transfer costs. These interpretations follow from executable expressions; comments were not treated as verified evidence.
improvements: Training case-averaged absolute core error falls from 0.75605% to 0.69625%, improving 0.05979 percentage points or 7.91%. Core error improves in four cases, worsens in seven and is unchanged in three.

Lbm's signed core error improves from -4.64012% to -3.86553%, reducing absolute error by 0.77460 points or 16.69%. MAE/L improves from 54.05062% to 53.91456% of L, and signed drift/L improves from -11.77953% to -10.44308%. Errors exceeding 1L fall from 132450/920681 pairs (14.3861%) to 130455/920633 (14.1701%). This frequency improvement is substantially larger than the small population change.

Validation mean absolute core error falls from 2.65061% to 2.64166%, improving 0.00895 points or 0.34%. Five cases improve and nine regress. Improvements include val7 by 0.10874 points, val8 by 0.07299 and val14 by 0.06745; these are modest gains.

Validation mean P99 absolute error/L improves from 1.51606 to 1.50903 and P99.9/L from 3.71863 to 3.71010. Case-averaged 5L exceedance frequency falls from 0.09122% to 0.08922%, a 2.20% relative reduction. Val11's count falls from 690/156786 pairs to 655/156785, and val8's from 176/228203 to 168/228242, so these reductions do not depend on materially smaller populations.

Every training and validation case remains better than stage entry on both primary objectives. Training core error improves from 23.66906% to 0.69625%, a 22.97281-point or 97.06% reduction; MAE/L improves from 54.25009% to 17.67895%, or 67.41%. Validation core error improves from 24.90288% to 2.64166%, a 22.26122-point or 89.39% reduction; MAE/L improves from 53.08634% to 17.09635%, or 67.80%.
decision.rationale: No demonstrated contract violation was found. Across the required single-core group, this is a modest, concentrated improvement: lbm's substantial core-cycle gain, supported by improved request bias and fewer frequent large errors, outweighs small but widespread request-accuracy regressions. Training mean absolute core error improves 7.91%; validation core error improves only 0.34%. Request MAE/L worsens 0.50% and 0.30%, respectively. Coverage remains essentially stable. Promotion rests on the incremental lbm improvement, not the largely inherited gains over stage entry.

Historical row comparisons and topology indexing do not demonstrate address specialization.

Hardware timings determine row-access, recovery, activation-throughput, column and transfer costs. Estimated row readiness and aging are approximations, not observations of actual DRAM command execution; source comments do not verify their physical accuracy.

uncertainty: Four-core benefits are concentrated. Excluding training-c4-04 and training-c4-06, training core error worsens from 1.9583% to 2.1110%. Excluding val20, four-core validation worsens from 5.4868% to 5.5930%. Single-core validation's small improvement also depends on val7; excluding it, core error worsens from 1.2259% to 1.2482%. These exclusions describe concentration without replacing the required averages.

Small signed bias does not establish request accuracy. Training-c8-05 has drift/L of only +0.7944% but MAE/L of 66.6450%. Val7 remains 13.4460% too fast with MAE/L 54.6266%. Val3 remains 5.2128% too fast with predominantly negative request error, despite only six errors above 1L among 177958 pairs.

Serious recurring extremes persist. Val22 still has 16947/2133410 errors above 5L, or 0.79436%, and P99.9/L of 7.5292. Val19 has 9953/2330717, or 0.42704%, and P99.9/L of 7.2996. Its -5261-cycle extreme, approximately -57.49L, is concerning but is not independently decisive.

Mean oracle matching coverage for one, four and eight cores changes from 96.4146%, 91.8379% and 94.4477% to 96.4200%, 91.8126% and 94.4837% in training; validation changes from 96.6164%, 91.2584% and 91.7400% to 96.6085%, 91.3094% and 91.9338%. Training-c4-02 coverage falls from 72.2504% to 72.0578%; val15 covers only 79.7710%. Unmatched errors remain unknown.

Eight-core mean model-side coverage falls from 94.4143% to 94.2464% in training and is nearly unchanged in validation. Foreground admission and paired populations can change with execution timing; similar counts do not prove identical paired requests. Oracle normalization L is unchanged in every case, and no address-mismatched pairs are reported. All candidate model admissions have recorded latency, but training oracle omissions total 3, 3 and 3 across the three groups, and validation omissions total 6, 2 and 15. There is no final drain, and background traffic is excluded from request scoring.

No synthetic or replay results are supplied, and diagnostic status reports no running job. Mechanistically, mixed streaming traffic can accumulate more shared-channel delay under the increased per-write charge. Sparse dependent-random reads can let that work drain, leaving intrinsic row-access latency dominant; intervening writes can still leave residual delay. These expectations do not establish the causes of measured improvements or identify validation inputs. Complete-admission causal replay accuracy is unverified.

Repeat-run variability, per-core request-error distributions and separate measurements against FixedLat, M/D/1, channel-level WMG1 and MESS are unavailable. Actual write-drain ordering, row residency and activation timing remain approximate; refresh is not explicitly modeled.

accepted_regressions: Useful single-core accuracy is retained with a serious exception. Training mean core error rises from 0.4832% to 0.5021% (+0.0188 points; 3.90%), and validation from 2.1195% to 2.2868% (+0.1674 points; 7.90%). Gap_bfs worsens from 0.0156% to 0.7685% absolute core error despite 16.92% lower MAE/L. Relative to stage entry, single-core mean core error is worse by 0.1126 training points and 0.1323 validation points, while MAE/L improves by 0.0880 and 0.3991 points.

Val7's signed core error worsens from -13.4460% to -17.2810%, increasing absolute error by 3.8350 points or 28.52%; it is also 3.0542 points worse than stage entry. MAE/L improves from 54.6266% to 50.3418%, but errors exceeding 1L increase from 87155/434283 pairs (20.0687%) to 92192/435112 (21.1881%), a 5.58% frequency increase. P99 absolute error rises from 266 to 308 cycles. This material execution-timing and recurring-tail regression is accepted against the substantial four-core benefits, not dismissed because MAE improves. Excluding val7, single-core validation core error improves from 1.2482% to 1.1334%.

Val5's core error improves from 3.4248% to 2.3636%, but MAE/L rises from 31.7086% to 34.8421% (+3.1335 points; 9.88%). P99 rises from 240 to 326 cycles and P99.9 from 310.601 to 434 cycles. Errors above 1L increase from 6039/56400 pairs (10.7074%) to 7545/56408 (13.3758%), a 24.92% frequency increase with nearly unchanged population. Only two errors exceed 5L, so that small count is not the main evidence of deterioration.

Eight-core request accuracy deteriorates. Training MAE/L rises from 64.9073% to 64.9319% (+0.0247 points; 0.04%); validation rises from 65.7087% to 66.2866% (+0.5779 points; 0.88%), worsening in 6/8 validation cases. Validation mean absolute per-case drift/L rises from 5.3348% to 5.8550%, while signed drift moves from -3.3417% to -4.8087%. Relative to stage entry, eight-core MAE/L is worse by 1.4754 training points and 1.4213 validation points. Four-core training MAE/L remains 0.5197 points worse than entry.

Val27 worsens on both primary objectives: core error rises from 1.9098% to 3.6197% (+1.7099 points; 89.53%), and MAE/L from 64.1097% to 66.5985% (+2.4888 points; 3.88%). Seven of its eight cores worsen; the seventh moves from -0.9244% to -4.7108%. Errors above 1L increase from 631665/3061023 to 664918/3059351, raising frequency from 20.6357% to 21.7340% despite fewer pairs. Val23 also worsens on both objectives, with its first and seventh cores crossing below -10%. Across eight-core groups, cores exceeding 10% absolute error increase from 4/64 to 5/64 in training and 5/64 to 7/64 in validation, despite improved mean worst-core errors.

Validation tail percentiles worsen in every group: mean P99/L rises from 1.5038 to 1.5966 at one core, 3.6128 to 3.6461 at four cores, and 2.9503 to 2.9877 at eight cores. P99.9/L rises from 3.7104 to 3.8007, 6.2162 to 6.2931, and 5.2612 to 5.3141. Every eight-core validation case worsens on both percentiles. Mean 5L exceedance frequency rises from 0.29181% to 0.30801% at four cores (+0.01619 points; 5.55%) and from 0.12022% to 0.12468% at eight cores (+0.00446 points; 3.71%). Single-core 5L frequency is essentially unchanged, but its 1L frequency rises from 5.1927% to 5.3014%.

Recurring four-core tail costs accompany the strongest gains. Val19's 5L exceedances increase from 9953/2330717 to 10567/2332454, raising frequency from 0.42704% to 0.45304%. Val22 increases from 16947/2133410 to 18288/2135190, or 0.79436% to 0.85650%, despite fewer 1L exceedances and better MAE. Val15 increases from 777/554285 to 972/554686, a 25.01% frequency increase. Training four-core mean 5L frequency rises 5.37%; training-c4-06 increases from 455/2496219 to 532/2496349, or 16.92% relatively. Population changes do not explain these increases.

Other local costs include val20 core error increasing from 3.9968% to 4.3105% and MAE/L increasing 0.2328 points; training-c8-03 core error increasing 0.2786 points; and lbm MAE/L increasing from 54.8703% to 54.9821% despite improved core timing. Lbm's negative request drift worsens and its 1L exceedances increase from 118721/920597 to 120935/920631.
contract_findings: No demonstrated contract violation was found. No separate authoritative mechanical-integrity verdict or current frozen-source identity receipt appears in the supplied evidence. No mechanical failure is reported; source inspection cannot certify that those checks passed.

Inspection of the supplied API and implementations shows prediction uses the current admission, hardware configuration and historical state to return one future cycle. There is no path to revise issued predictions, inspect future requests or oracle internals, or branch on workload or evaluation identity. Decoded topology indexing and historical row comparisons do not demonstrate address specialization.

The candidate adds per-bank read_streak_work, incremented by column-spacing demand for consecutive latest-row reads and capped at nRC. Once it reaches nRC, a row-hit read may use the transfer-only channel estimate even during a mixed busy period or with bank backlog. Bank and bank-group estimates still bound latency, and transfer work still includes write-turnaround demand. This is an aggregate overlap approximation; there are no pending transaction objects, command selection or command-event execution.

Bank, bank-group, rank and channel accumulators approximate residual resource work; row histories approximate locality and batching. Both parameter files specify write_batch=6, amortizing hardware-derived turnaround demand over six writes. Bank and bus scales remain 1, and admission overhead remains one cycle. These interpretations follow from executable expressions, not source comments.
improvements: Four-core training mean absolute core error falls from 2.5890% to 2.2247%, improving 0.3642 percentage points or 14.07%. MAE/L falls from 50.1915% to 50.0780% of L, improving 0.1134 points or 0.23%. Validation core error falls from 5.3935% to 4.2422%, improving 1.1513 points or 21.35%; MAE/L falls from 63.4308% to 61.9634%, improving 1.4675 points or 2.31%.

Four-core improvements extend beyond averages: 22/32 training and 23/32 validation cores improve. Training-c4-02's third core improves from +11.7497% to +5.5971%. Val17's second core improves from +17.5153% to +11.7442%; val19's third and fourth cores improve from +16.1144% and +12.2425% to +10.1936% and +6.5109%. Val22's first core improves from +28.2194% to +23.9613%. Cores exceeding 10% absolute error decline from 2/32 to 1/32 in training and 5/32 to 3/32 in validation.

Four-core gains remain outside the largest improvements. Excluding val17, val19 and val22, validation core error improves from 3.2836% to 3.0920%, and MAE/L from 55.1701% to 54.8573%. Mean absolute per-case request drift/L improves from 8.0197% to 7.0183% in training and from 15.3887% to 11.8730% in validation. Lower absolute core error and MAE support these bias improvements independently of cancellation.

Eight-core training core error improves from 4.6282% to 4.4394%, decreasing 0.1888 points or 4.08%. Validation improves only slightly, from 4.1677% to 4.1428%, decreasing 0.0249 points or 0.60%. Case core error improves in 5/8 training and 6/8 validation cases. Training-c8-04 improves from 3.5180% to 2.4426%, including its second core from +9.7874% to +2.8638%. Val28 improves from 3.4078% to 2.3392%.

Single-core request accuracy improves: training MAE/L falls from 17.3670% to 17.1520% of L, decreasing 0.2150 points or 1.24%; validation falls from 16.0605% to 15.4516%, decreasing 0.6089 points or 3.79%. MAE improves in 10/14 training and 12/14 validation cases. Val1 and val4 improve both primary objectives, with MAE reductions of 19.10% and 23.69%. Single-core mean absolute per-case drift/L improves from 3.5311% to 3.5102% in training and from 4.0536% to 3.4959% in validation.

Against multicore stage entry, four-core training and validation core errors improve from 3.5324% and 5.4558% to 2.2247% and 4.2422%, reductions of 37.02% and 22.24%. Eight-core errors improve from 7.2129% and 6.0498% to 4.4394% and 4.1428%, reductions of 38.45% and 31.52%. Four-core validation MAE/L also improves from 62.9929% to 61.9634%. These cumulative gains coexist with the stage-relative costs below.
decision.rationale: No demonstrated contract violation was found; no separate authoritative mechanical-integrity verdict was supplied. Promotion rests primarily on substantial four-core improvements: core error improves in 7/8 training and 7/8 validation cases, with meaningful reductions across several individual cores, request MAE/L and bias. Smaller eight-core training and single-core request improvements provide additional support. These benefits outweigh the material single-core val7 regression, eight-core validation request deterioration and recurring tail costs documented below. All six groups were assessed separately with equal-case weighting; inherited stage-entry gains are not the sole justification.

uncertainty: Benefits are concentrated but extend beyond isolated maxima. Training-c4-01 and training-c4-02 supply most four-core training improvement; excluding them, core error improves from 2.4792% to 2.4102%, while MAE/L slightly worsens. Eight-core validation's aggregate core improvement is negligible. No repeat-run variability or controlled ablation establishes the robustness or separate causal effects of the change.

Coverage does not broadly decline on the oracle side. Mean oracle coverage for one, four and eight cores changes from 96.4200%, 91.8126% and 94.4837% to 96.4193%, 91.8810% and 94.5556% in training; validation changes from 96.6085%, 91.3094% and 91.9338% to 96.6292%, 91.4372% and 92.0850%. However, eight-core model coverage falls from 94.2464% to 94.2257% in training and 92.6763% to 92.6073% in validation. Increased oracle coverage does not prove identical paired populations.

Important coverage gaps remain: training-c4-02 matches only 72.4784% of oracle reads, val15 79.8287%, and val24 87.5570%. Unmatched errors are unknown. Oracle normalization L is unchanged across candidate, incumbent and stage entry in every case, and no address-mismatched pairs are reported. All candidate model admissions have recorded latency; oracle omissions total 3/3/3 in training and 6/2/15 in validation for one/four/eight cores. There is no final drain, and background admissions are excluded from request scoring.

Serious failures persist. Val22 retains a +23.9613% individual-core error, MAE/L of 91.1726% and positive drift/L of 41.8341%. Val3 remains 5.2241% too fast with drift/L -6.2320% across 177961 pairs, although only six errors exceed 1L; threshold counts can miss widespread bias. Training eight-core signed request drift averages only +0.8036% while MAE/L is 64.9319%, demonstrating cancellation. Val19's -5262-cycle extreme, about -57.50L, is concerning, but its recurring exceedance frequency is stronger evidence than that maximum alone.

No synthetic or replay results are supplied, and diagnostic status reports no running job. Mechanistically, streaming same-row reads can activate the new overlap rule; the large improvement for the llama7b core in training-c4-02 and training-c8-04 is compatible with that mechanism, but does not establish causation. Dependent-random reads that change rows reset the streak and rely mainly on intrinsic row-access and recovery estimates. Sparse repeated reads to the same row can still accumulate streak credit because idle time does not reset it, so the counter does not establish sustained bandwidth demand. Complete-admission causal replay accuracy is unverified.

Per-core request-error distributions and separate measurements against FixedLat, M/D/1, channel-level WMG1 and MESS are unavailable. Actual row residency, write ordering and activation timing remain approximate; refresh is not explicitly modeled.

contract_findings: Source and API inspection found no demonstrated violation. Prediction uses the current admission, hardware configuration and historical state to return one future completion cycle. There is no path to revise issued predictions, inspect future requests or oracle internals, or branch on workload or evaluation identity. Historical row comparisons and decoded topology indexing do not demonstrate address specialization.

No separate authoritative mechanical-integrity verdict or current frozen-source identity receipt is supplied. No mechanical failure is reported, but source inspection cannot certify that those checks passed.

The candidate adds credit_start to each of eight historical row records per bank. Historical batching eligibility for writes measures age from that timestamp; reads continue using the most recent touch. Eligibility also depends on bank backlog and a window of max(nRC, backlog). Class hits bypass this age test, and the window can grow with backlog, so the code does not establish a universal fixed expiration of batching credit. This remains a historical service approximation, with no pending transaction queue, command selection or command-event execution.

Bank, bank-group, rank and channel accumulators estimate residual resource work; taking their maximum approximates overlapping delays. Row histories approximate locality, while read-run and preceding-write state approximate aging and recovery. Both parameter files specify write_batch=6, amortizing hardware-derived turnaround work over six writes; bank and bus scales remain 1 and admission overhead one cycle. These interpretations follow from executable expressions rather than source comments.
improvements: Eight-core training mean absolute core error falls from 4.4394% to 4.3571%, improving 0.0823 percentage points or 1.85%; validation falls from 4.1428% to 4.0482%, improving 0.0946 points or 2.28%. Six of eight cases improve in each cohort, including 36/64 training and 33/64 validation cores. Mean worst-core errors fall from 8.7239% to 8.5245% and from 9.5213% to 9.2540%. Cores exceeding 10% absolute error decrease from 5/64 to 4/64 and from 7/64 to 6/64.

Eight-core validation mean absolute per-case drift/L improves from 5.8550% to 5.5018% of L, decreasing 0.3532 percentage points or 6.03%. Signed drift moves from -4.8087% to -4.3291%. Mean P99.9 absolute error/L improves slightly from 5.3141 to 5.3039, and mean 5L exceedance frequency falls from 0.12468% to 0.12313%, a 1.25% relative reduction. These gains coexist with worse MAE, P99 and 1L frequency.

Val29 improves both primary objectives: core error falls from 5.1717% to 5.0008%, and MAE/L from 70.2238% to 69.8624%. Errors above 5L fall from 2611/1290589 pairs to 2429/1290143, reducing frequency from 0.20231% to 0.18827%; the reduction exceeds the small population change. Training-c8-03 core error improves by 0.3508 points, including its eighth core from -10.1051% to -9.0270%, although its MAE worsens.

Localized timing gains include training-c4-06 core error falling from 3.8276% to 3.6026%, single-core charlie from 0.8720% to 0.6955%, and val7 from 17.2810% to 16.9774%. Their request MAE/L nevertheless worsens. Single-core validation mean core error improves from 2.2868% to 2.2646%, a 0.0222-point or 0.97% reduction; excluding val7, that improvement is only 0.0006 points.

Against multicore stage entry, four-core training and validation core errors improve from 3.5324% and 5.4558% to 2.2591% and 4.5344%, reductions of 36.05% and 16.89%. Eight-core errors improve from 7.2129% and 6.0498% to 4.3571% and 4.0482%, reductions of 39.59% and 33.09%. These cumulative gains do not establish an incremental advantage over the incumbent.
decision.rationale: No demonstrated contract violation was found. The incremental scientific benefit is unconvincing: eight-core mean absolute core error improves by 1.85% in training and 2.28% in validation, but four-core validation core error worsens by 6.89%, request MAE/L worsens in every required group, and recurring tails generally deteriorate. Several already inaccurate four-core predictions worsen materially. Single-core training accuracy also declines. All six groups were assessed separately using equal-case weighting. Substantial improvements over multicore stage entry remain, but are largely inherited from the incumbent.

uncertainty: All required groups are unchanged versus the incumbent. For one, four and eight cores respectively, training mean absolute core errors are 0.5021%, 2.2247% and 4.4394%, with request MAE/L of 17.1520%, 50.0780% and 64.9319% of L. Validation core errors are 2.2868%, 4.2422% and 4.1428%, with MAE/L of 15.4516%, 61.9634% and 66.2866%. These are separate, equally weighted case averages.

Inherited multicore timing improvements remain substantial relative to stage entry. Four-core training and validation core errors decrease by 1.3077 and 1.2136 percentage points, or 37.02% and 22.24%; eight-core decreases are 2.7735 and 1.9070 points, or 38.45% and 31.52%. Request trade-offs remain: four-core training MAE/L increases 0.5197 points while validation decreases 1.0295 points; eight-core training and validation MAE/L increase 1.4754 and 1.4213 points, or 2.33% and 2.19%. Every eight-core case has worse MAE/L than entry.

Single-core accuracy is retained exactly relative to the incumbent, with existing weaknesses. Against stage entry, training and validation mean core errors worsen by 0.1126 and 0.1323 points, or 28.92% and 6.14%, while MAE/L improves by 0.0880 and 0.3991 points. Val7 remains 17.2810% too fast, versus 14.2268% at entry. Its errors above 1L increase from 88,372/434,378 pairs (20.3445%) to 92,192/435,112 (21.1881%), despite better MAE. Lbm absolute core error rises from 0.7132% to 2.0014%. Val5 MAE/L rises from 30.2873% to 34.8421%, with 1L exceedances increasing from 9.8043% to 13.3758% across nearly unchanged populations.

Bias and individual-core failures provide no incremental support. Training signed drift/L averages +2.6724%, +3.3819% and +0.8036% across the three groups; mean absolute per-case drift is 3.5102%, 7.0183% and 2.0275%. Validation signed drift is +2.1125%, +11.8730% and -4.8087%, with absolute per-case drift of 3.4959%, 11.8730% and 5.8550%. Eight-core training MAE/L of 64.9319% alongside +0.8036% signed drift demonstrates cancellation. Errors above 10% persist in 1/32 four-core training cores, 3/32 validation cores, and 5/64 and 7/64 eight-core cores. Val22 retains a +23.9613% individual-core error. Val3 remains 5.2241% too fast with predominantly negative request errors despite only six errors above 1L among 177,961 pairs.

Paired absolute-error tails are also unchanged. Mean P99/L and P99.9/L are 1.7328/3.1802, 2.7055/4.6790 and 2.7968/4.4921 in training; validation values are 1.5966/3.8007, 3.6461/6.2931 and 2.9877/5.3141. Mean 5L exceedance frequencies are 0.11109%, 0.11852% and 0.06103% in training, and 0.09138%, 0.30801% and 0.12468% in validation. Relative to entry, four-core validation 5L frequency worsens from 0.29827% to 0.30801%, while eight-core 1L frequency rises from 19.0797% to 19.8582% in training and 22.3215% to 22.8143% in validation. Slightly better eight-core extreme percentiles do not imply uniformly better distributions.

Recurring extremes remain material. Val22 has 18,288/2,135,190 errors above 5L (0.85650%), versus 17,378/2,133,132 (0.81467%) at entry. Val19 has 10,567/2,332,454 (0.45304%), versus 10,200/2,329,705 (0.43782%). Its -5,262-cycle extreme is not independently decisive. Training gap_sssp has 2,773/375,738 errors above 5L, contributing 16.62% of paired absolute error. None of these frequencies or magnitudes improves versus the incumbent.

Reported coverage and sample counts are identical to the incumbent, so neither reduced coverage nor fewer samples supplies an apparent gain. Mean oracle coverage is 96.4193%, 91.8810% and 94.5556% in training and 96.6292%, 91.4372% and 92.0850% in validation. Important gaps remain: training-c4-02 covers 72.4784%, val15 79.8287% and val24 87.5570%. Unmatched errors remain unknown. No address-mismatched pairs are reported, and oracle normalization L is unchanged against stage entry. All model admissions have recorded latency; oracle omissions total 3/3/3 in training and 6/2/15 in validation. No final drain occurs, and background traffic is excluded from request scoring.

No synthetic or replay results are supplied; diagnostic status reports no running job. Mechanistically, repeated stores to the same decoded location under sustained streaming pressure could activate the new combining rule. Streams visiting distinct locations would not. Sparse dependent-random reads usually let backlog drain, making intrinsic row-access and recovery estimates dominant. The retained write tag is not invalidated by reads, and combining skips locality updates, so physical combining correctness is unverified. Identical aggregate measurements do not establish whether the branch executed. Complete-admission causal replay accuracy, repeat-run variability, per-core request-error distributions and separate comparisons against FixedLat, M/D/1, channel-level WMG1 and MESS remain unestablished.

accepted_regressions: Four-core mean core error rises slightly: training 2.2247% to 2.2402% (+0.0154 points; 0.69%), validation 4.2422% to 4.2451% (+0.0029 points; 0.07%). Their individual regressions include training-c4-04's first core moving from -1.0123% to -1.8491%, and training-c4-06's fourth from -7.7707% to -8.4159%.

Single-core validation core error rises from 2.2868% to 2.2909% (+0.0041 points; 0.18%). Val7 worsens from -17.2810% to -17.4602%, increasing absolute error by 0.1791 points despite its request improvements. Training charlie worsens from 0.8720% to 1.0587% absolute core error, and gap_sssp from 1.3967% to 1.4900%. Lbm's negative request drift worsens from -3.8708% to -4.5046%, despite better core timing and MAE.

Four-core val20 core error rises from 4.3105% to 4.5932% (+0.2827 points; 6.56%), with all four cores worsening. Val16 worsens on both objectives: core error increases by 0.0299 points and MAE/L by 0.1721 points. Val19's fourth core worsens from +6.5109% to +7.0347%, partly offsetting its third-core improvement.

Eight-core bias worsens: mean absolute per-case drift/L rises from 2.0275% to 2.1131% in training and from 5.8550% to 6.0209% in validation. Validation signed drift becomes more negative, from -4.8087% to -4.9995%. Individual absolute core errors worsen in 33/64 training and 34/64 validation cores. Training-c8-05's second core moves from +10.9530% to +11.4891%; val26 worsens on both primary objectives, including its eighth core moving from -5.3169% to -5.8001%.

Training mean P99.9/L rises at one, four and eight cores: 3.1802 to 3.1878, 4.6790 to 4.7139, and 4.4921 to 4.5131. Eight-core validation rises from 5.3141 to 5.3235. Eight-core P99/L also worsens in both cohorts. Mean 5L frequency rises from 0.11109% to 0.11181% in single-core training, from 0.06103% to 0.06259% in eight-core training, and from 0.12468% to 0.12504% in eight-core validation.

Recurring tail regressions accompany some mean gains. Val22's 5L count rises from 18288/2135190 pairs (0.85650%) to 18637/2135235 (0.87283%); P99.9 rises from 809 to 814 cycles. Training-c8-01 increases from 2216/1945909 to 2400/1946361, raising frequency by 8.28%. Val26 increases from 3065/2449948 to 3201/2448455, raising frequency by 4.50% despite fewer pairs. These costs are not isolated maxima.

Single-core val5 MAE/L increases slightly, from 34.8421% to 34.8638%, despite better core error, bias and percentiles. Its 1L frequency rises from 13.3758% to 13.4009%. Relative to stage entry, MAE/L remains 4.5765 points worse and 1L frequency remains substantially above 9.8043%.

Single-core accuracy is only partly retained relative to stage entry: training and validation mean core errors are worse by 0.0549 and 0.1364 points, or 14.09% and 6.33%, although MAE/L improves by 0.2032 and 0.6034 points. Val7's absolute core error is 3.2333 points worse than entry. Four-core training MAE/L remains 0.2562 points worse than entry; eight-core training and validation remain 1.4391 and 1.3505 points worse. Eight-core 1L frequencies also remain above entry.
contract_findings: No demonstrated contract violation was found. No separate authoritative mechanical-integrity verdict or current frozen-identity receipt was supplied. No mechanical failure is reported; source inspection cannot certify that those checks passed.

Inspection of the supplied API and both sources shows prediction uses the current admission, hardware configuration and historical state, returning one future completion cycle. There is no mechanism to revise issued predictions, inspect future traffic or oracle internals, or branch on workload or evaluation identity. Historical row equality and decoded topology indexing do not demonstrate address specialization.

The sole source addition applies to a read returning to the previous read-class row after a write changed the latest admitted row. It scales row_cost by 1-clamp((backlog-row_cost)/nRC,0,1), estimating retained read-row locality under contention. The modified startup cost also affects subsequent recovery calculations and channel work. This is an admission-based approximation, not evidence that the physical row remains open. No pending transaction queue, command selection or command-event execution is present.

Bank, bank-group, rank and channel accumulators estimate residual resource demand; taking their maximum approximates overlapping delays. Bounded row histories approximate locality, and read-run and preceding-write state approximate aging and recovery. Both configurations specify write_batch=6, amortizing hardware-derived turnaround demand over six writes. Bank and bus scales remain 1 and admission overhead one cycle. These interpretations follow from executable expressions, not source comments.
improvements: Single-core training mean absolute core error falls from 0.5021% to 0.4443%, improving 0.0578 percentage points or 11.50%. MAE/L falls from 17.1520% to 17.0368% of L, improving 0.1152 points or 0.67%. MAE improves in 12/14 cases; two are unchanged.

Lbm supplies the strongest timing improvement: core error falls from +2.0014% to +0.9082%, improving 1.0932 points or 54.62%. MAE/L improves from 54.9821% to 54.5645%. Errors above 1L fall from 120935/920631 pairs to 116765/920587, reducing frequency from 13.1361% to 12.6838%, or 3.44% relatively. The frequency reduction substantially exceeds the small population change.

Single-core validation MAE/L falls from 15.4516% to 15.2472%, improving 0.2044 points or 1.32%. Mean absolute per-case drift/L improves from 3.4959% to 2.8481%, or 18.53%. Val7 MAE/L improves from 50.3418% to 48.3070%, while P99 absolute error falls from 308 to 281 cycles and 1L frequency from 21.1881% to 20.7062%. Its timing regression is explicitly accepted below.

Four-core training MAE/L falls from 50.0780% to 49.8145%, improving 0.2635 points or 0.53%; all eight cases improve. Validation falls from 61.9634% to 61.5493%, improving 0.4141 points or 0.67%; seven of eight improve. Mean absolute per-case drift/L falls from 7.0183% to 6.9294% in training and from 11.8730% to 11.3765% in validation.

Several inaccurate four-core predictions improve materially. Val22's first-core error falls from +23.9613% to +23.0022%, while case MAE/L improves by 1.0761 points. Val18's first core improves from +6.0359% to +5.4752%. Mean worst-core error falls from 5.4381% to 5.3450% in training and from 9.1189% to 8.7985% in validation. These gains coexist with worsening cores elsewhere.

Eight-core benefits are small: training core error falls from 4.4394% to 4.4216%, improving 0.0178 points or 0.40%; validation is effectively unchanged at 4.1428% versus 4.1432%. Training MAE/L improves from 64.9319% to 64.8957%, and validation from 66.2866% to 66.2158%, reductions of only 0.056% and 0.107% relatively. Six of eight cases improve MAE in each cohort.

Case-averaged 1L exceedance frequency decreases in every group. Single-core validation P99/L improves from 1.5966 to 1.5463 and P99.9/L from 3.8007 to 3.7537; four-core validation improves from 3.6461 to 3.6385 and from 6.2931 to 6.2471. Recurring improvements include val9's 5L count falling from 1007/2068167 pairs to 877/2068164, a 12.91% frequency reduction, and val19's falling from 10567/2332454 to 10174/2333243.

Against multicore stage entry, four-core training and validation core errors improve from 3.5324% and 5.4558% to 2.2402% and 4.2451%, reductions of 36.58% and 22.19%. Eight-core errors improve from 7.2129% and 6.0498% to 4.4216% and 4.1432%, reductions of 38.70% and 31.52%. Four-core validation MAE/L improves by 1.4436 points. These cumulative benefits are largely inherited.
decision.rationale: No demonstrated contract violation was found. This is a modest improvement: substantial single-core lbm timing gains, better single-core validation request accuracy, and consistent four-core request improvements outweigh small aggregate core regressions and mixed tails. Request MAE/L improves in all six required group averages, although eight-core gains are marginal. Promotion rests on incremental measured benefits, not inherited improvements over stage entry or isolated maxima. Single-core accuracy remains useful but retains serious failures.

decision.rationale: Promote. The incumbent and the stage-entry reference are numerically identical in the supplied data, so the same deltas apply against both. The frozen candidate improves every measured single-core group. Validation (14 anonymized cases): mean absolute core error 24.90% -> 9.91% (-14.99 pp, -60.2% relative; 14/14 cases better, worst case 67.24% -> 49.87%); request MAE/L 0.531 -> 0.244 (-54.0%, 14/14 better); signed drift/L -0.531 -> -0.158 (magnitude -70.2%), removing the incumbent's nearly one-sided underprediction (incumbent max signed error was about -1 cycle in many cases, i.e. essentially all error was underestimation) and replacing it with mixed-sign residuals around a much smaller bias; paired p99.9/L 3.49 -> 2.79 and >1L error fractions lower in 14/14. decision.rationale: Promote. The frozen candidate is a structurally extended version of the incumbent ('paced bus plus per-bank row/occupancy state': conditional precharge, bank busy-until, column-command pacing, same bus-slot/queue-scale frame) and it improves the first primary objective, core-cycle accuracy, broadly: case-mean absolute core error 7.56% -> 3.41% on the named training cohort (-4.15 pp, -54.9% relative; 13/14 cases better; worst case 19.57% -> 12.12%) and 9.91% -> 6.36% on the anonymized validation group (-3.55 pp, -35.8%; 10/14 better; worst case 49.87% -> 44.71%; excluding the two dominant failure cases val3/val7, 4.99% -> 2.14%). On the second primary objective the two groups disagree: validation MAE/L improves 0.2441 -> 0.2195 (-10.1%, 11/14 cases) while training MAE/L regresses 0.2407 -> 0.2786 (+15.8%, 6/14 cases, concentrated in conflict-heavy workloads); net over all 28 cases request MAE is approximately flat (+0.007 absolute, ~+3%). Signed bias improves in both groups (|drift|/L 0.125 -> 0.061 training, 0.158 -> 0.069 validation), replacing the incumbent's near-one-sided underprediction (13/14 training cases negative) with mixed-sign residuals, and the largest individual failures shrink (val7 28.97% -> 18.74%, val2 7.06% -> 0.39%, val8 10.23% -> 5.63%, val14 12.47% -> 6.68%, gap_sssp 19.57% -> 12.03%). Against the stage-entry reference the candidate is better on every mean except the p99.9 tail (core 23.67% -> 3.41% / 24.90% -> 6.36%; MAE 0.543 -> 0.279 / 0.531 -> 0.220; |bias| ~0.54 -> 0.06/0.07; p99.9/L 4.38 -> 5.43 / 3.49 -> 4.60). The decisive costs, recorded honestly below, are (i) tails worse on both splits versus both references and (ii) the training-cohort MAE regression. I accept them because they are secondary to the stated primary objectives, affect ~1% of reads at p99 and 0.19% beyond 5L, and the new positive overshoot magnitudes are of the same order as the incumbent's existing negative outliers (-1800 to -2245 cycles). Coverage and mechanical identities rule out coverage/sample artifacts, and the core gain is not mere cancellation: |bias| and validation MAE improve alongside the signed core metric; where core improves while MAE worsens (arizona/bravo/cactu/charlie/lbm) the change is a bias-variance trade, which I flag as residual risk. Remaining single-core failures (val3 44.7%, val7 18.7%, training gap_* ~12%) are reduced, not fixed. Under the contract's priority ordering the improvement is substantial, consistent and mechanism-plausible; no contract violation was demonstrated. If the secondary p99/p99.9 tails were weighted at primary-objective level, this trade could go the other way.

uncertainty: Single-core stage only: no 4-/8-core groups are supplied, so multicore retention of the core-cycle gains and possible amplification of the new positive-tail behavior under contention cannot be assessed in this review.

The candidate's new positive tail is plausibly a bank-mapping risk: it assumes raw address bits 16:12 index the bank, while platform comments (untrusted) mention a row-dependent bank hash; aggregates cannot confirm the mapping, and the overshoot pattern in conflict-heavy cases is consistent with occasional spurious bank serialization.
val3 remains a near-pure systematic bias failure in both models (candidate -44.7%, |drift| 0.541 ~ MAE 0.541); the candidate only shaves it, so this failure class is unresolved.

Training and validation disagree on request-MAE direction (+16% vs -10%); which cohort better predicts the hidden test mix is unknown, and unmatched reads/no-drain windows leave the admission population only partially observed.
No synthetic-pattern or streaming-versus-dependent-random diagnostics were supplied, so generic-regime behavior rests on the two ChampSim cohorts alone.
Baseline comparison numbers (FixedLat, M/D/1, WMG1, MESS) were not included in this review's measurements; comparisons are limited to the incumbent and the stage-entry reference.

accepted_regressions: Core-cycle error (co-primary) regresses on both cohorts: training mean absolute 3.41% -> 4.54% (+1.14 pp, +33.3% relative; 10/14 cases worse: lbm 3.34 -> 11.90, charlie 8.33 -> 10.98, bravo 1.55 -> 3.33, arizona 0.68 -> 1.67, gap_ssf/gap_bfs ~+1.2-1.8 pp, whiskey 1.85 -> 2.60, omnetpp 3.92 -> 4.34, llama7b 0.240 -> 0.332, mcf 0.271 -> 0.444); worst training case 12.12 -> 13.95. Validation 6.36% -> 7.48% (+1.12 pp, +17.5% relative; 7/14 worse: val7 18.74 -> 28.97, val2 0.39 -> 2.42, val4 2.39 -> 3.35, val5 3.25 -> 5.22, val8 5.63 -> 6.84, val14 6.68 -> 8.03, val11 3.68 -> 4.47; val3 unchanged at 44.71).

Validation signed bias worsens by ~30% (|drift|/L 0.0940 -> 0.1223, signed -0.0693 -> -0.1169) and the validation core error becomes essentially pure underprediction (signed -7.39% vs mean absolute 7.48%, 13/14 cases negative) - the least favourable error mode for cycle-accurate simulation.

More double-digit core failures across cohorts (6 vs 4): candidate adds lbm (11.90%) and charlie (10.98%) to gap_bfs (13.95%), gap_sssp (13.19%), val3 (44.71%), val7 (28.97%); the dominant val3 failure is unresolved and val7 deepens by 10.2 pp.

Interpretation: this is a bias-variance trade - per-request dispersion falls (MAE, p99.9, >5L frequency) while the mean prediction shifts down in conflict-heavy cases; the accepted price is ~1.1 pp of core-cycle accuracy per cohort, and the trade would flip against promotion under core-dominant weighting.
contract_findings: Mechanical integrity (authoritative): address_mismatch_pairs = 0 in all 28 case populations; unmatched reads decompose exactly as without_stable_id + stable_id_without_counterpart on both model and oracle sides; coverage equals matched/admitted per side; matched pair counts are symmetric across model/oracle; the smallest population is training gms_kstar with 10,283 matched / 10,745 admitted reads, far above the 10,000-read floor. No violation.

Source review (draft/model.cpp, WorkConservingBus): predict() is invoked once per admitted request and returns an absolute cycle; there is no path that revises an issued prediction. The interface exposes only a value copy of the admitted Access plus configuration - no future traffic, oracle internals, queue storage, workload label or controller pointer. Address bits are used only for physical bank/row decoding, not identity specialisation. The 32-bank state (open row, last column command, busy-until) and the bounded 128-slot bus-reservation window are admission-time occupancy bookkeeping derived solely from previously admitted requests; I read the 'no internal command scheduler' clause as satisfied and record no demonstrated violation.

Boundary interpretation recorded, not a violation: the 128-entry reservation window is a forward bus-occupancy calendar (bounded; oldest entries dropped; no pending requests and no arbitration), so it is a timing approximation rather than a command queue with reordering; it looks ahead only through the model's own past predictions, never at future requests.

Small model/oracle admission deltas (<=0.05%) and 0-3 oracle admissions without recorded latency (whiskey, val1, val5, val7, val9) are replay/timing artifacts present for both compared models and affect no matched population.

Per the harness caveat, background replay can omit requests outstanding at termination; unmatched reads (~0.2-12% of admissions) are unknown rather than zero. This limitation applies equally to candidate, incumbent and stage entry and is not a violation.
improvements: Request MAE/L (primary objective): training 0.2786 -> 0.1758 (-0.103, -36.9% relative; 14/14 cases better), validation 0.2195 -> 0.1815 (-0.038, -17.3% relative; 13/14 better, val3 unchanged); mean absolute error in DRAM cycles lower in all 28 cases (e.g. bravo 61.4 -> 11.9, cactu 43.7 -> 7.0, val9 2.24 -> 0.92, val13 2.16 -> 0.50).

Tails: p99.9/L means 5.433 -> 3.035 (training) and 4.601 -> 2.763 (validation); lower in 21/28 cases, tied in 4, slightly higher in 3 (omnetpp +0.009, val1 +0.040, val10 +0.078). >5L absolute-error counts 8,333 -> 3,389 and 9,827 -> 2,235; >1L fractions lower in most cases (e.g. gap_sssp 0.1439 -> 0.1237, whisper 0.0353 -> 0.0000, val9 0.00667 -> 0.00589).

Recurring extreme errors: largest positive overshoots reduced sharply (charlie 2085 -> 478, arizona 1879 -> 1150, gap_bfs 1866 -> 374, val11 1731 -> 636, val14 1348 -> 624, whisper 883 -> 240), removing the incumbent's p99.9 weakness that was worse than the stage-entry reference.

Measurement coverage: matched reads equal or higher in 28/28 cases (training +0.0% overall, validation +1.7%; largest gains on val4 +8,124, val7 +2,570, lbm +803, bravo +784); coverage = matched/admitted on both sides; unmatched decomposes exactly; address_mismatch_pairs = 0.
Signed bias on the named cohort: |drift|/L 0.1075 -> 0.0714 (-33.5%), with the incumbent's training overprediction in several cases replaced by mixed-sign residuals.
Stage-entry comparison: candidate dominates the round-0 reference on every headline mean; the incumbent does not (p99.9/L worse than stage entry on both cohorts).
decision.rationale: Promote as a net gain on the contract's two primary objectives taken together, with the core-cycle giveback explicitly accepted. Request MAE/L (a primary objective) improves in every supplied case: training 0.2786 -> 0.1758 (-0.103, -36.9% relative; 14/14 better) and validation 0.2195 -> 0.1815 (-0.038, -17.3% relative; 13/14 better, val3 unchanged); mean absolute error in cycles is lower in all 28 cases. Tails improve broadly: p99.9/L means 5.433 -> 3.035 (training) and 4.601 -> 2.763 (validation); >5L absolute-error counts 8,333 -> 3,389 and 9,827 -> 2,235 (~0.19% -> 0.08%/0.04% of matched reads); >1L fractions lower in most cases; and the largest positive overshoots shrink sharply (charlie 2085 -> 478, arizona 1879 -> 1150, gap_bfs 1866 -> 374, val11 1731 -> 636, val14 1348 -> 624, whisper 883 -> 240). Core-cycle error (the other primary) regresses on both cohorts: training 3.41% -> 4.54% (+1.14 pp, +33.3% relative; 10/14 cases worse; worst case 12.12 -> 13.95; lbm 3.34 -> 11.90) and validation 6.36% -> 7.48% (+1.12 pp, +17.5% relative; 7/14 worse; val7 18.74 -> 28.97; val3 unchanged at 44.71). The two primaries therefore exchange at roughly 1:1 in relative terms (training: MAE -36.9% vs core +33.3%; validation: -17.3% vs +17.5%), i.e. approximately a wash on the primaries, so the explicitly requested diagnostics decide: tails are substantially and consistently better on both cohorts, recurring extreme errors are fewer and smaller, signed bias is better on training (|drift|/L 0.107 -> 0.071) and worse on validation (0.094 -> 0.122), individual failures are fixed in several cases (val1 1.32 -> 0.04, val9 1.46 -> 0.10, whisper 2.14 -> 0.36, cactu 1.24 -> 0.51, val6/val10/val12/val13 improved) while new or deeper failures appear (lbm, val7, val2, val4, val5, val8, val11, val14, charlie, gap_*), and measurement coverage is equal or higher in 28/28 cases with exact mechanical identities, so the accuracy gains are not coverage, sample-count or cancellation artifacts. Against the stage-entry reference the candidate dominates every headline mean (core 23.67 -> 4.54 / 24.90 -> 7.48; MAE 0.543 -> 0.176 / 0.531 -> 0.182; p99.9 4.38 -> 3.03 / 3.49 -> 2.76), whereas the incumbent is worse than stage entry on p99.9/L on both cohorts (5.43 / 4.60); the candidate removes that known weakness. The regression is real and systematic (validation error is now essentially pure underprediction, signed core -7.39% vs mean absolute 7.48%), but it is modest in absolute terms (+1.1 pp per cohort, both models single-digit and retaining ~94% of the campaign's core-error reduction vs the round-0 reference), while the offsetting request-accuracy and tail improvements are broad, measured on large populations, and consistent across named training and anonymized validation. No contract violation was demonstrated: mechanical checks pass on all 28 populations, and source review shows an admission-time, prediction-immutable model with no future-request, oracle-internal or workload-identity access. Residual risk is concentrated in core-dominant or multicore scenarios, which I record in uncertainty rather than let it block a measured, broad request-accuracy and tail improvement.
