contract_findings: No demonstrated contract violation. Mechanical integrity checks are authoritative and pass identically for candidate and incumbent on all 28 supplied case populations: address_mismatch_pairs = 0 everywhere; unmatched reads decompose exactly as without_stable_id + stable_id_without_counterpart on both model and oracle sides (e.g. arizona 3033 = 2833 + 200); coverage = matched/admitted per side; matched pair counts are symmetric across model/oracle; the smallest population, training gms_kstar, has 10,283 matched / 10,745 admitted reads, far above the 10,000-oracle-read floor.

Source review of the frozen candidate (draft/model.cpp, WorkConservingBus): predict() is called once per admitted request and returns an absolute DRAM cycle; no path revises an issued prediction. The supplied interface exposes only a value copy of the admitted Access plus static configuration, with no future traffic, oracle internals, queue storage, workload label or live controller pointer; address bits are used only for physical bank/row decoding, as in the incumbent.

The bounded 128-slot reservation window remains a forward bus-occupancy calendar over the model's own previously issued bookings (no pending requests, no arbitration or reordering). I read it as an admission-time timing approximation rather than an internal command scheduler; recorded as an interpretation, not a violation.

The candidate's only difference from the incumbent is inert state: five per-bank fields written but never read (row_is_write, last_access_was_write, last_access_time, last_write_time, write_busy_until) plus comment edits. Dead field writes violate no listed prohibition, but they also cannot change behaviour, which is why every candidate metric equals the incumbent's.

Small model/oracle admission-count deltas (<=0.05%) and 0-3 oracle admissions without recorded latency (whiskey, val1, val5, val7, val9) are replay/timing artifacts, identical for both compared models, and touch no matched population.

Per the harness caveat, background replay can omit requests outstanding at termination; unmatched reads (~0.1-12% of admissions) are unknown rather than zero. This limitation applies equally to candidate, incumbent and stage entry and is not a violation.

uncertainty: Single-core stage only (group 1 supplied): no 4-/8-core or multicore-round data, so multicore retention of the incumbent's accuracy cannot be assessed in this round.

The candidate and incumbent measurement blocks are bit-identical in every field; source analysis explains this as prediction equivalence, but the review bundle contains no separate candidate identity or configuration block, so a duplicated comparison cannot be fully excluded from the data alone. Under either explanation there is no demonstrated improvement to justify promotion.

The incumbent's unresolved single-core failures are unchanged by the candidate: val3 remains near-pure underprediction at 44.71 pp core error (|drift|/L 0.5411 vs MAE/L 0.5412), val7 28.97 pp, training gap_bfs 13.95 pp / gap_sssp 13.19 pp / lbm 11.90 pp, with rare deep under-shoots (val14 -2248 cycles, lbm -1743).

The incumbent itself carries the round-3 accepted trade (higher core error than the model it replaced, better request MAE and tails); this candidate neither improves nor worsens that trade, so the retained risk profile is unchanged.

Unmatched reads at window boundaries are unobserved (0.1-12% of admissions), so their error contribution is unknown, and no synthetic streaming/dependent-random or replay diagnostics were supplied; the assessment rests on the two supplied ChampSim cohorts.

accepted_regressions: Request MAE/L regresses on both cohorts: training 0.1758 -> 0.1806 (+0.0048, +2.7% relative; worse in 10/14 cases, equal 4, better 1); validation 0.18151 -> 0.18218 (+0.0007, +0.37%; worse 8/14, better 3, equal 3). Broad but shallow (largest case arizona +0.0295, +8.5%; charlie +0.0144; val2 +0.0063; val11 +0.0047), caused by the same upward latency shift that removes the aggregate bias.

Tail metrics mixed: validation p99.9/L 2.763 -> 2.785 (+0.8%; val9 2.04 -> 2.42, val2 2.21 -> 2.38, val12 2.23 -> 2.30) and the composite tail mean is marginally higher on both cohorts (1.3364 vs 1.3357 training; 1.2985 vs 1.2972 validation), even though >5L counts fall and training p99.9/L edges down; the candidate moves some reads from far-tail undershoots into mid-range overshoots (e.g. arizona >1L fraction 0.126 -> 0.146 while >5L falls 191 -> 147, extreme_max 1,150 unchanged).

Individual-case regressions where the incumbent was already unbiased or over-predicting: whisper is worse on every metric (core 0.364% -> 0.475%, MAE 0.0753 -> 0.0811, p99.9/L 2.28 -> 2.54); val9 core 0.100% -> 0.168% with p99.9/L 2.04 -> 2.42 (small absolute); val12 core 0.2645 -> 0.2731; val4 3.346 -> 3.361; val10 0.25564 -> 0.25584. None creates a new failure class or a double-digit error.

Concentration: about 91% of the training core-mean gain comes from lbm (excluding it, training core improves only -1.7%), and the dominant validation failures are essentially unmoved (val3 44.71% unchanged; val7 28.97% -> 28.76%). The candidate does not address the worst unresolved underprediction (val3, val7, gap_bfs ~13.9%, gap_sssp ~13.0%), so the core benefit does not generalize uniformly.
contract_findings: No demonstrated violation. Mechanical integrity checks (authoritative) pass on all 28 case populations for both models: address_mismatch_pairs = 0 everywhere; unmatched reads decompose exactly as without_stable_id + stable_id_without_counterpart on both model and oracle sides; coverage = matched/admitted per side; matched pair counts are symmetric; the smallest population (gms_kstar) has 10,283 matched / 10,745 admitted reads, far above the 10,000-read floor.

Source and parameter review (draft/model.cpp + draft/parameters.json vs references/incumbent/*): predict() is invoked once per admitted request and returns an absolute cycle with no revision path; the interface exposes only a value copy of the admitted Access plus configuration (no future traffic, oracle internals, controller state, or workload label); address bits are used only for bank/row decoding. The bus reservation window is the incumbent's admission-time occupancy calendar, not a command scheduler, and the candidate's only behavioural delta is write_extra 6 -> 10 (write bus span 14 -> 18 cycles); the other new parameters/bookkeeping (write_wait_scale, drain_conflict_extra, drain_window_cycles, row_from_write, row_from_write_time) are gated off at the frozen values (0/0.0), and all parameters are inside their declared ranges.

Small model/oracle admission-count deltas (<=0.05%) and 0-3 oracle admissions without recorded latency (whiskey, val1, val5, val7, val9) are replay/timing artifacts common to candidate, incumbent and stage entry, and touch no matched population.

Per the harness caveat, the no-drain replay can omit requests outstanding at termination; unmatched reads (0.1-12% of admissions) are unknown rather than zero. This limitation applies equally to all compared models and is not a violation.
improvements: Core-cycle accuracy (primary objective) improves on both cohorts: training mean absolute core error 4.545% -> 3.845% (-0.70 pp, -15.4% relative; 9/14 cases better, 4 tied, 1 worse); validation 7.480% -> 7.416% (-0.064 pp, -0.86%; 7 better / 3 tied / 4 worse; excluding val3/val7, 2.587% -> 2.530%, -2.2%).

Largest trainable failure fixed at no local per-request cost: training lbm core error 11.90% -> 3.00% (-74.8% relative) with unchanged MAE (0.5869 -> 0.5872), improved p99.9/L (3.30 -> 3.06) and fewer >5L errors (50 -> 37); the incumbent's systematic underprediction there (|drift|/L 0.1214) is essentially removed (0.0006). Per-case mean-cycle shifts scale with write intensity (lbm +31.6, charlie +7.0, arizona +5.4, val7 +2.4, val5 +2.0; zero on val3/val6/gms_*/llama7b/mcf), consistent with the write-bus mechanism.

Signed bias improves on both cohorts: |drift|/L 0.0714 -> 0.0613 (training, -14.1%) and 0.1223 -> 0.1177 (validation, -3.8%), moving the residual centre toward zero (training signed drift -0.0606 -> -0.0428). This is a bias reduction, not a narrower per-request distribution; MAE does not fall with it.

Large-error frequency and magnitude: >5L absolute-error counts 3,389 -> 3,155 (training) and 2,235 -> 2,179 (validation); the deepest negative excursions shrink where the change engages (lbm -1,743 -> -1,714 cycles; val5 -493 -> -439; val8 -743 -> -685; val14 -2,248 -> -2,207), and training p99.9/L edges down (3.035 -> 3.017).

Measurement coverage is unchanged or greater: matched reads within about +/-0.03% of the incumbent in all 28 cases (e.g. val9 2,068,312 vs 2,068,204; lbm 920,523 vs 920,582); coverage = matched/admitted on both sides; address_mismatch_pairs = 0, so gains are not coverage or sample-count artifacts.

Stage-entry comparison: the candidate beats the round-0 reference on every headline mean (core 23.67% -> 3.85% / 24.90% -> 7.42%; MAE/L 0.5425 -> 0.1806 / 0.5309 -> 0.1822; p99.9/L 4.38 -> 3.02 / 3.49 -> 2.78), whereas the incumbent is slightly worse than the candidate on core, |drift| and >5L counts.
decision.rationale: Promote on a small but genuinely positive net change, with the request-MAE cost accepted explicitly. A diff of the supplied sources and frozen parameters shows the candidate's only behavioural difference from the incumbent is a larger write-drain bus span (write_extra 6 -> 10, i.e. 14 -> 18 bus cycles per posted write); its added parameters and bookkeeping (write_wait_scale, drain_conflict_extra, drain_window_cycles, row_from_write fields) are inert at the frozen 0/0.0 values and all parameters are inside declared ranges, so every measured difference traces to write-bus occupancy. Core-cycle error (primary) improves on both cohorts: training 4.545% -> 3.845% (-0.70 pp, -15.4% relative; 9/14 cases better, 4 tied, 1 worse; worst case 11.90% -> 3.00%), validation 7.480% -> 7.416% (-0.064 pp, -0.86%; 7 better / 3 tied / 4 worse; 2.587% -> 2.530%, -2.2%, excluding val3/val7). The training gain concentrates in lbm, where a systematic aggregate underprediction is removed with no per-request cost (MAE 0.5869 -> 0.5872, p99.9/L 3.30 -> 3.06, >5L errors 50 -> 37), and per-case mean-latency shifts scale with write intensity (lbm +31.6, charlie +7.0, arizona +5.4, val7 +2.4, val5 +2.0 cycles/read; zero on val3, val6, gms_*, llama7b, mcf), which matches the mechanism. Request MAE/L (the other primary) regresses slightly on both cohorts (training 0.1758 -> 0.1806, +2.7%, worse in 10/14; validation 0.18151 -> 0.18218, +0.37%, worse in 8/14), but the penalty is shallow (largest single case arizona +0.030, +8.5% relative), while |drift|/L improves (-14.1% / -3.8%), >5L absolute-error counts fall (3,389 -> 3,155; 2,235 -> 2,179), p99.9/L is flat (-0.6% / +0.8%), matched populations/coverage are unchanged, and no new failure class appears. The two dominant validation failures (val3 44.7%, val7 28.8%) are unmoved, which caps the benefit; the promotion therefore rests on the contract's allowance for a small regression supported by meaningful improvements, and would flip under strong request-MAE dominance or if the write-heavy core benefit did not transfer. Against the stage-entry reference the candidate dominates every headline mean (core 23.67% -> 3.85% / 24.90% -> 7.42%; MAE/L 0.5425 -> 0.1806 / 0.5309 -> 0.1822; p99.9/L 4.38 -> 3.02 / 3.49 -> 2.78; |drift| ~0.54 -> 0.061 / 0.118). No contract violation is demonstrated: mechanical integrity checks pass on all 28 populations for both models, and source review shows one immutable prediction per admitted request with no future-request, oracle-internal, or workload-identity access.

The validation-cohort core gain is small (-0.064 pp, -0.86%) and thin (7 better / 4 worse / 3 tie) and is dominated by the two large unchanged failures; if the hidden workload mix is not write-heavy, the real benefit could shrink toward the -1.7%/-2.2% residual or to zero while the +0.4% to +2.7% MAE giveback still applies.

contract_findings: Mechanical integrity checks (authoritative) pass on all 28 case populations for both models: address_mismatch_pairs = 0 everywhere; unmatched reads decompose exactly as without_stable_id + stable_id_without_counterpart on both model and oracle sides; coverage = matched/admitted per side; matched pair counts are symmetric across model/oracle; the smallest population (gms_kstar) has 10,283 matched / 10,745 admitted reads, above the 10,000-read floor. No violation demonstrated.

Source review: predict() is called once per admitted request and returns an absolute cycle with no revision path; the supplied interface exposes only a value copy of the Access plus static configuration (no future traffic, oracle internals, controller pointer or workload label); address bits are used only for bank/row decoding; no workload/address/evaluation identity specialisation. The bounded 128-slot bus reservation calendar is admission-time occupancy bookkeeping over the model's own prior predictions, with no pending-request queue and no reordering/arbitration; I read it as a timing approximation rather than an internal command scheduler and record no demonstrated violation.

The candidate's delta versus the incumbent is parameters-only: identical 10,718-character model.cpp; drain_conflict_extra 0 -> 90 and drain_window_cycles 0 -> 250 are the only differences, both within declared ranges, and the added term is a reported-only scalar (it never feeds back into bank or bus timelines), so it cannot compound.

Replay caveats: small model/oracle admission deltas (<0.05%) and 0-3 oracle admissions without recorded latency (whiskey, val1, val5, val7, val9) are replay/timing artifacts common to both models; unmatched reads (~0.1-12% of admissions; no final drain) are unknown, not zero, and this limitation applies equally to candidate, incumbent and stage entry.
improvements: Core-cycle accuracy (primary objective) improves on both cohorts: training mean absolute core error 3.845% -> 0.796% (-3.05 pp, -79.3% relative; 11/14 cases better, 1 tie, 2 worse; worst case 13.93% -> 3.62%); validation 7.416% -> 2.187% (-5.23 pp, -70.5%; 8 better, 5 worse, 1 unchanged; worst 44.71% -> 15.84%); the gain persists excluding the two dominant validation failures (2.53% -> 0.84%).

Request MAE/L (primary objective) improves on both cohorts: training 0.1806 -> 0.1739 (-3.7%) and validation 0.1822 -> 0.1578 (-13.4%); absolute error in cycles falls most where the incumbent was worst (val3 122.2 -> 43.8 cycles; gap_bfs 21.9 -> 12.0; gap_sssp 37.7 -> 31.3).

Signed bias largely removed: |drift|/L 0.0613 -> 0.0290 (training; signed -0.0428 -> +0.0095) and 0.1177 -> 0.0540 (validation; signed -0.1120 -> -0.0400); residual per-case signs are mixed rather than one-sided underprediction.

Dominant failure modes fixed: val3 44.71 -> 15.84, val7 28.76 -> 4.71, val11 4.42 -> 0.11, val14 7.96 -> 1.38, val8 6.80 -> 1.05, val5 4.76 -> 1.57, val4 3.36 -> 1.28, gap_sssp 13.05 -> 0.90, gap_bfs 13.93 -> 2.72, charlie 10.56 -> 0.89, omnetpp 4.33 -> 0.33, whiskey 2.58 -> 0.02; double-digit training failures drop from 3 to 0 and validation from 2 to 1.

Recurring large errors are less frequent: >5L absolute-error counts 3,155 -> 3,033 (training) and 2,179 -> 1,827 (validation); >1L counts 310,440 -> 272,773 and 224,326 -> 187,520; top extreme magnitudes comparable or smaller (gap_sssp 1,376 -> 1,121 cycles; lbm 1,369 -> 1,318; val14 -2,207 -> -2,211).

Measurement quality is not the source of the gain: matched reads differ from the incumbent by -0.74% (training) and -0.13% (validation) overall, within +/-0.7% in 25/28 cases (exceptions lbm -3.1%, val2 -1.1%, val12 -0.9%), with zero address mismatches and exact population identities.
decision.rationale: Promote. The frozen candidate is the incumbent with one approximation enabled: the same 10,718-character model.cpp, and parameters differing only in drain_conflict_extra (0 -> 90) and drain_window_cycles (0 -> 250), both within declared ranges. It improves both primary objectives on both cohorts. Core-cycle error (case-mean absolute): training 3.845% -> 0.796% (-3.05 pp, -79.3% relative; 11/14 cases better, 1 tie, 2 worse; worst case 13.93% -> 3.62%) and validation 7.416% -> 2.187% (-5.23 pp, -70.5%; 8 better, 5 worse, 1 effectively unchanged; worst 44.71% -> 15.84%; excluding val3/val7, 2.53% -> 0.84%). Request MAE/L: training 0.1806 -> 0.1739 (-3.7%) and validation 0.1822 -> 0.1578 (-13.4%). Signed bias improves sharply (|drift|/L 0.0613 -> 0.0290 training and 0.1177 -> 0.0540 validation; training signed drift -4.28% -> +0.95%), replacing the incumbent's one-sided underprediction, and the gains land exactly on the incumbent's dominant underprediction failures (val3 44.71 -> 15.84, val7 28.76 -> 4.71, gap_sssp 13.05 -> 0.90, gap_bfs 13.93 -> 2.72, charlie 10.56 -> 0.89, val14 7.96 -> 1.38, val11 4.42 -> 0.11, val8 6.80 -> 1.05, lbm 3.00 -> 1.26), consistent with the bank drain-serialisation effect the term approximates. Large-error frequency falls (>5L counts 3,155 -> 3,033 training and 2,179 -> 1,827 validation; >1L 310,440 -> 272,773 and 224,326 -> 187,520) and no training case remains double-digit (three did). Costs are small and recorded below: p99.9/L 3.017 -> 3.115 (training, +3.3%) and 2.785 -> 2.909 (validation, +4.5%); training p99/L 1.336 -> 1.423 (+6.5%) with validation p99/L flat (1.299 -> 1.294); plus small regressions in already-accurate cases (arizona 1.43 -> 3.62, whisper 0.475 -> 0.904, val2 2.29 -> 2.95, val1 0.02 -> 0.35, val9 0.17 -> 0.47, val12 0.27 -> 0.56, val10 0.26 -> 0.33), none creating a new failure class. Coverage and mechanical identities hold (address_mismatch_pairs = 0 everywhere, exact unmatched decompositions, coverage = matched/admitted, matched symmetric, smallest case 10,283 matched / 10,745 admitted), and overall matched populations change only -0.74% (training) and -0.13% (validation), so the gains are not sample-loss or cancellation artifacts: MAE and |drift| fall together, and signed core error falls alongside mean-absolute core error. Against the stage-entry reference the candidate dominates every headline mean (core 23.67 -> 0.80 training / 24.90 -> 2.19 validation; MAE 0.543 -> 0.174 / 0.531 -> 0.158; p99.9/L 4.38 -> 3.12 / 3.49 -> 2.91; |drift|/L ~0.54 -> 0.03 / 0.05). Under the contract's priority ordering (core and MAE primary, small regressions acceptable when supported by substantial improvements), this is a large, broad, mechanism-plausible gain; no contract violation was demonstrated.

A promotion must identify a demonstrated improvement; there is none on either primary objective (core-cycle accuracy, request MAE/L) nor on signed bias, tails, individual-core failures, or measurement coverage. Against the stage-entry reference the retained incumbent carries the campaign's gains (training core 23.669% -> 0.796%, MAE/L 0.5425 -> 0.1739, p99.9/L 4.377 -> 3.115, |drift|/L 0.5425 -> 0.0290; validation 24.903% -> 2.187%, 0.5309 -> 0.1578, p99.9/L 3.493 -> 2.909, |drift|/L 0.5309 -> 0.0540), while the candidate adds no measurable benefit over the incumbent. uncertainty: write_extra is a single global constant: the multicore gain is bought by making every posted write cheaper on the bus (18 -> 10 cycles), which costs the write-heavy 1-core case lbm (14.06% underprediction) and likely c4-04. If the hidden test mix is more single-core write-heavy than the supplied cohorts, the core-error trade could reverse; the request-level evidence (MAE/L improved in 24/24 multicore cases and most single-core cases) is more robust than the core-level evidence.

Single-core retention: flat on the anonymized validation cohort (2.19% -> 2.21%) with MAE improving, but degraded on the named training cohort (0.80% -> 1.75%; ex-lbm 0.76% -> 0.81%). A previous round tuned write_extra 6 -> 10 specifically to fix lbm, so this round partially reverses a previously accepted calibration and the campaign has now moved this constant in both directions.

Tails: p99.9/L and >5L counts are slightly worse in most groups; differences are small in absolute terms (<= about 0.02% of matched reads at 5L) but consistent in direction, with no offsetting tail improvement except validation 1-core.

val3 remains the campaign's largest failure (15.84% core error, near-pure underprediction) and is untouched by both models; the underprediction failure class is reduced but not eliminated (val7 4.94%, val28 4.48%, val2 2.75%, lbm 14.06%).

Mechanism attribution rests on the parameter delta and the case-level pattern (bit-identical write-inactive cases; shifts concentrated in write-heavy cases), not on per-request traces, synthetic streaming/dependent-random diagnostics or controlled replay experiments, which were not supplied for this round.

Per-case metrics are conditional on the matched subpopulation (no-drain windows; unmatched errors unknown), and FixedLat / M/D/1 / channel-level WMG1 / MESS baselines were not included in the supplied measurements, so comparisons here are limited to the incumbent and the stage-entry reference (which are numerically identical).

accepted_regressions: Request MAE/L (second primary) regresses in all six groups: 0.1641 -> 0.1726 (+5.2%), 0.4978 -> 0.5180 (+4.1%), 0.6513 -> 0.6602 (+1.4%), 0.1550 -> 0.1578 (+1.8%), 0.5792 -> 0.5995 (+3.5%), 0.6650 -> 0.6730 (+1.2%); mean +2.5%. It remains better than the stage-entry reference in 5 of 6 groups and equal in the sixth.

4-core validation core error regresses 6.44% -> 6.77% (+5.1%), driven by val17/val19/val22 (about 10.9/12.3/10.3%) partly offset by val15/val16/val20; the validation cohort group-mean core error is +1.6% (2 of 3 groups improve).

Worst individual-core errors worsen in all four multicore groups (8-core training 21.5 -> 23.8 pp, 8-core validation 17.2 -> 19.7 pp, 4-core training 19.3 -> 22.8 pp, 4-core validation 27.0 -> 31.8 pp) and double-digit case failures rise 2 -> 5; the new ones are marginal (10.2-12.3%) and error frequency beyond 5L still falls, so this is recorded as a moderate giveback rather than a new failure class.
The dominant validation failure val3 (15.84%, near-pure underprediction, |drift|/L 0.190 vs MAE/L 0.194) is unchanged, and val7 barely moves (4.94 -> 4.71).
contract_findings: Mechanical integrity (authoritative): all checks pass on all 28 case populations - address_mismatch_pairs = 0 everywhere; unmatched reads = without_stable_id + stable_id_without_counterpart exactly on both model and oracle sides; coverage = matched/admitted per side; matched pair counts symmetric across model/oracle; the smallest population (training gms_kstar) has 10,283 matched / 10,745 admitted reads, above the 10,000-read floor.

Source/behavioural review: the candidate is an admission-time predictor - predict() runs once per admitted request and returns an immutable absolute cycle; the interface exposes only the admitted Access plus static configuration (no future traffic, oracle internals, controller state, or workload label); address bits are used only for bank/row decoding; the bounded reservation calendar is occupancy bookkeeping over the model's own prior predictions (no pending requests, no reordering or arbitration), recorded as an interpretation of the 'no internal command scheduler' clause, not a demonstrated violation. The behavioural delta is confined to the write path: write-inactive cases (val3, val6, val13, gms_kstar, gms_maxclique, llama7b, mcf, cactu, omnetpp, whisper) are bit-identical across candidate, incumbent, and stage entry, inconsistent with workload, address, or evaluation-identity specialisation.

Replay caveats apply equally to both models and are not violations: admission-count deltas at or below 0.05%, 0-3 oracle admissions without recorded latency (whiskey, val1, val5, val7, val9), and unmatched reads (no final drain) unknown rather than zero.

Group-mean core error 4.39% -> 4.23% (-3.6%); multicore mean -2.7%; training mean -9.1%.

Stage-entry comparison: candidate better on 10 of 12 group means (one equal, one worse - 1-core training core error) - 8-core training core 11.72% -> 6.06% (-48%), 8-core validation 8.87% -> 4.98% (-44%), 4-core training 4.08% -> 3.94%, 4-core validation 6.94% -> 6.77%, and request MAE/L better in 5 of 6 groups and equal in the sixth (8-core training 0.719 -> 0.660; 8-core validation 0.724 -> 0.673).

Tails: paired p99.9/L lower than the incumbent in 5 of 6 groups (incumbent +0.7% to +5.2% above stage entry in five groups; candidate within 0 to +4.6% of it), and >5L absolute-error counts fall in the multicore groups (8-core training 12,016 -> 11,519; 8-core validation 25,048 -> 24,422), recovering the round-11 tail giveback.
Signed bias: mean |drift|/L 0.081 -> 0.079, better in 4 of 6 groups (1-core training/validation and both 8-core groups), with residual signs mixed rather than one-sided underprediction.

Single-core retention (multicore-round requirement): 1-core core accuracy is retained or improved (training -18%, validation flat at 2.19 vs 2.21), while 1-core request MAE gives back a small amount (training 0.1641 -> 0.1726; validation 0.1550 -> 0.1578).

Coverage/mechanical quality: matched populations differ from the supplied references by at most about 0.1% per case with the same coverage identities; address_mismatch_pairs = 0 everywhere; unmatched reads decompose exactly into without_stable_id + stable_id_without_counterpart - the accuracy changes are not coverage or sample-count artifacts.

Core-cycle accuracy (first primary) improves in five of six groups: 1-core training 1.75% -> 1.44% (-0.31 pp, -18%, partially repairing the incumbent's lbm underprediction, -14.1% -> -10.2%), 4-core training 4.35% -> 3.94% (-9.4%), 8-core training 6.49% -> 6.06% (-6.6%), 1-core validation 2.21% -> 2.19%, 8-core validation 5.07% -> 4.98% (-1.8%); only 4-core validation regresses (6.44% -> 6.77%, +5.1%). Group-mean core error 4.39% -> 4.23% (-3.6%); multicore mean -2.7%; training mean -9.1%. Request MAE/L (second primary) regresses in all six groups (mean 0.452 -> 0.464, +2.5%; per-group +1.2% to +5.2%) but remains better than the stage-entry reference in five groups and equal in the sixth, so the giveback does not erase the campaign's request-accuracy gains. Secondary diagnostics split and, on balance, favour the candidate: paired p99.9/L is lower than the incumbent in 5 of 6 groups (the incumbent sat +0.7% to +5.2% above the stage entry in five groups while the candidate is within 0 to +4.6%), >5L absolute-error counts fall in the multicore groups (8-core training 12,016 -> 11,519; 8-core validation 25,048 -> 24,422), and mean |drift|/L improves 0.081 -> 0.079 with residual signs mixed. The costs, recorded below, are an MAE giveback in every group, a 4-core validation core regression, worse worst-individual-core errors in all four multicore groups (21.5 -> 23.8, 17.2 -> 19.7, 19.3 -> 22.8, 27.0 -> 31.8 pp), and double-digit case failures rising 2 -> 5 (the new ones marginal, 10.2-12.3%, while error frequency beyond 5L still falls). Against the stage-entry reference the candidate is better on 10 of 12 group means (one equal, one worse - 1-core training core error) - e.g., 8-core training core 11.72% -> 6.06%, 8-core validation 8.87% -> 4.98%, and request MAE/L better in 5 of 6 groups. Coverage and mechanical integrity are intact (address_mismatch_pairs = 0 in all 28 populations; unmatched reads decompose exactly; coverage = matched/admitted; matched populations within a fraction of a percent), so the gains are not coverage or sample-loss artifacts. Under the contract's allowance for small regressions supported by meaningful improvements elsewhere, the broad core improvement (including the multicore groups this stage targets, plus the single-core core recovery), together with better tails and bias, outweighs the small request-MAE giveback; no contract violation is demonstrated.

decision.rationale: Keep the incumbent. The frozen candidate is the incumbent's exact source (draft/model.cpp is character-identical to references/incumbent/model.cpp, 13,988 characters, WorkConservingBus) with one parameters.json delta: busy_center 0.7 -> 0.8 and busy_tau 10000 -> 40000, i.e. the write-drain batching gate is pushed toward the slow/isolated-drain endpoint in mid-occupancy regimes. On the named training cohort that helps the first primary objective: case-mean absolute core error falls in all three groups (1c 1.4357 -> 1.0678 pp, -25.6%; 4c 3.9409 -> 3.3462, -15.1%; 8c 6.0642 -> 5.6403, -7.0%; pooled training 3.814 -> 3.351 pp, -12.1%), driven mainly by lbm (10.18 -> 5.07 pp) and its two 4-core mixes (c4-04 7.95 -> 5.21, c4-06 7.89 -> 5.57). Diagnostics mostly improve on the training side: paired p99.9/L and the composite tail fall slightly in 5 of 6 groups, |drift|/L falls in 4 of 6, and the per-case worst-core average improves in both training multicore groups (4c 10.11 -> 9.23, 8c 18.96 -> 18.69). However, on the anonymized validation cohort — the only generalization evidence — both primary objectives regress: core error rises in both multicore groups (4c 6.766 -> 6.883 pp, +1.7%; 8c 4.978 -> 5.442, +9.3%; 1c unchanged at 2.1873) and request MAE/L rises in all six groups (pooled 0.4635 -> 0.4705, +1.5%). The training gain is concentrated rather than broad: excluding lbm the training 1-core error is 0.760 vs 0.763 pp (no gain), and the training 4-core gain lives entirely in the two lbm-containing cases (the other six each regress slightly, +0.02 to +0.09 pp); the training 8-core gain is broader (6/8 cases better) but the held-out 8-core loss (val23 +2.68, val27 +2.43, val28 +1.48 pp) more than offsets it. Worst-case health does not improve: the largest individual core errors grow in training 8c (23.8 -> 27.1 pp at c8-04; c8-07 21.9 -> 26.7; c8-01 21.8 -> 25.5) and in validation (val28 19.7 -> 22.3, val22 31.8 -> 33.5, val23 9.3 -> 14.0, val25 8.7 -> 13.9), the mean per-case worst-core worsens on both validation groups (4c 14.41 -> 15.03, 8c 11.31 -> 12.75), and >1L paired-error counts rise in several groups (training 8c +3.6%, validation 8c +2.7%) even though p99.9/L improves slightly. So the candidate is a global write-bus recentering whose sign flips between the named cohort (favourable) and the held-out cohort (unfavourable), with request MAE giving back everywhere: the improvements are not substantial or broadly replicated enough to displace the incumbent under the contract's 'unconvincing benefit' rule. The candidate does retain single-core accuracy (training improves, validation unchanged) and remains clearly ahead of the stage-entry reference on both primaries in all four multicore groups (e.g. training 8c 11.72 -> 5.64, validation 8c 8.87 -> 5.44; MAE/L better in 6/6 groups), so if the hidden mix is more write-heavy/training-like than the validation cohort this judgment could reverse. No contract violation is demonstrated.

Both models dominate the stage-entry reference on the multicore groups this stage targets (8-core training core 6.08 vs 11.72; 8-core validation 4.96 vs 8.87; 8-core MAE 0.660/0.672 vs 0.719/0.724), but those gains are already held by the incumbent and the candidate adds nothing measurable. The dominant residual failures are untouched: val3 15.84% core with near-pure underprediction (|drift|/L 0.190 vs MAE/L 0.194), lbm 10.17%, val19 11.99%, val22 10.40%, val17 10.94%, c4-04 7.96%, c4-06 7.95%, c8-08 7.82%, c8-02 7.31%, val7 4.71%, with deep single-read outliers still present (val19 -5,260 cycles, val27 -5,204, c8-02 -4,440). Mechanical integrity passes on every population and no contract violation is demonstrated, so there is no integrity reason to act; because the candidate shows no material improvement on either primary objective or on bias/tails/individual failures, and the two primaries move at roughly +/-0.1% in opposite directions between cohorts, the benefit is unconvincing and the incumbent is retained.

provenance.baseline_sources:
# Baseline sources

| Baseline | Source | Implementation in this repository |
|---|---|---|
| FixedLat | gem5 v25.1.0.0 `SimpleMemory` (7a2b0e41) and zsim `SimpleMemory` (f524c056), as the abstraction | `fixed_lat_controller.cpp`: constant read latency (42 DRAM cycles for DDR5-4800) with an internal 8-cycle bandwidth queue; requests are accepted immediately, not rejected and retried as in gem5 |
| M/D/1 | zsim `MD1Memory` (f524c056, GPL-2.0) | `md1_controller.cpp`: port of `MD1Memory::updateLatency`/`access`; latency = zero-load latency x (1 + rho / (2 (1 - rho))), access counts smoothed per 10,000-cycle phase, smoothing 0.5 |
| WMG1 | Sniper windowed M/G/1 queue (56505e42) | `ramulator/ext/sniper_wmg1`: Sniper's `computeQueueDelay`, `addItem`, `removeItems` with a clock adapter; 10-us window quantized to 24,038 DRAM cycles, 8-cycle service |
| Mess | Mess simulator, standalone (7feba12c, BSD-3-Clause) | `ramulator/ext/mess`: upstream `MessMemCtrl` compiled directly; a loader patch reads the bandwidth-latency curve (`mess_DDR5.txt`, calibrated on the cycle-level oracle without refresh); one predictor per channel, 1,000-access window |

All four baselines count reads and writes toward load, acknowledge writes immediately and return reads at their predicted departure. They model no finite admission queue, command scheduling, refresh or bank conflicts. Predictions start at `controller_clock + 1`.
